chapters.title: Spirit Codex
chapters.text:
This book explains how to build and use Tribal Power. Start with a small workshop, then add automatic power, item transport and equipment.

How the camp works
1. Pulse is stored energy. A generator makes it: Drumheart (hand or redstone beats), Pulse Resonator (catalyst plus totems), Ley Collector (landscape), or a later tribe craft.
2. Put the generator within 8 blocks of the machine that spends Pulse. Distant or unloaded generators cannot help. Machines draw from generators first, then from totem buffers a Conductor has filled.
3. Most workshops also need a matching Resonance Totem within 8 blocks. The totem is an elemental requirement, not a generator. Missing voices pause work and spend nothing.
4. Neighbour machines pass items when touching faces are set to Output into Input. Hoppers do the same job. Relays are for distance. Fluid uses a Spirit Cistern to store and a Tide Pump or fluid relay to move.
5. A held redstone signal pauses work; stored Pulse, items and fluid stay. Crouch and right-click this book on a silent machine to hear why.
6. Walkthroughs list Goal, You need, Steps and Check. Open one when you want a shopping list instead of a summary.

Words this book uses
Pulse — stored energy.
Voice / attunement — the element a totem provides: Earth, Fire, Water, Air, Spirit, or Loom.
Keeping — whether a totem is Answered (active), Dim, or Quiet. Quiet can pause new work even when Pulse is full.
Rank — an upgrade you cook into a machine or tool in Echo Attune, then Bind, then Manifest. Faster work costs more Pulse per second; Pulse per craft stays about even.
The March — the other dimension. Charge a Gate Drum and empty-handed use it to walk through; do not strike it like a Drumheart.

Start here
1. Read First camp. Make a Drumheart and store some Pulse.
2. Read Echo workshops, Shatter, then Walkthrough: smelt in an Ember Kiln.
3. Read Walkthrough: seat a Resonator to make automatic power.
4. The Walkthroughs category is the full camp: generators, workshops, patterns, voices, rites, camp hands and March structures have a Goal, a shopping list and a Check.

Using this book
Search by item or machine name. Click Recipes to see the current recipe; click an ingredient to follow its recipe. If JEI is installed, a JEI button and right-click on an item open the same recipes there. Use Bookmark to save a page and Back to return. Next follows the beginner lessons. Scroll to read long pages.

Diagrams
Item pictures can open recipes. Right-click them for JEI when it is installed. Placement diagrams show a build from above, one layer at a time. Turn Motion off, then Step or Left/Right to inspect.

When something stops
Hold this book, crouch and right-click the machine. Its diagnostic message explains missing power, parts or ingredients. Later discoveries stay hidden until you unlock them or choose Spoilers. Story pages are collected under The old world.

chapters.title: The world that was
chapters.text:
Before the void had a name, the sky was a floor. Nine Strands — Soil, Stone, Sprout, Claw, Spark, Clock, Swarm, Sigil, Spindle — were pulled taut by nine tribes. Continents hung from that lattice the way fruit hangs from a well-kept vine. Weather ran along it. Rain knew where to fall. Nothing dropped that was not meant to.

Roads were sung into the thread and walked. Crops rooted into Strand as much as soil. Drums under one pad were heard as Pulse under another. The Loom was not a god and it was not a machine. It was nine agreements kept at once. When the tribes pulled together, the horizon stayed put. That is the whole of the old physics.

From that pull came this craft: Pulse, lattice, seal, and the road into the March. The engines are still out there. Orphaned, humming, sacred. Treat them like an inheritance, not a scrap pile.

chapters.title: When the agreements failed
chapters.text:
Something severed the Loom. This Codex does not know what. Neither did the tribes, by the end. One moment the sky was a floor. The next, the agreements failed in the same breath.

The Pad-keepers felt it first — hearths went cold while the sky still looked whole. Then the Rootbinders' living anchors held for a season, and that season is why anything is still up here. Guardians snapped in their arenas. Songs kept playing with nobody to hear them. Gate-paths stayed open into nowhere.

The Cut was not a war. It was a knot coming undone. Continents fell in the space of a drum-roll. What did not fall is a pad of earth the Strands still remember. You are standing on leftovers that learned how to be a floor.

chapters.title: What mending means
chapters.text:
You are not putting continents back. You are teaching nine voices to agree again, one camp at a time.

A chalk link is a promise. A seated catalyst is a conversation restarted. A tablet rite is asking politely, smaller than the old world asked.

The March kept the halls, the drums, the tablets. Read every tablet. Strike the Silent Drum when you are ready. Tell the camps we are sorry it took so long. The world does not snap back. It learns to hold.

chapters.title: Continents of thread
chapters.text:
A continent was a pad that had forgotten it was a pad. Fields ran because Soil ran with them. Rivers kept manners because Sprout taught water where to sit. Cities did not float. They hung, and hanging felt like standing.

Roads were sung, not cut. Pulse under one hearth was heard as Pulse under the next. Night was an appointment the Seal-carvers kept. Storms were a Drumheart argument walked back before dawn.

You can still see the habit in the aurora. It is the sky trying to remember a schedule.

chapters.title: Nine arguments
chapters.text:
No tribe could hold the sky alone. Soil without Stone is warmth with nowhere to stand. Spark without Clock is a beat with no song. Sigil without Spindle is a promise with no road home.

The old world was not peace. It was maintenance. Eight pulls became eight arguments. The cloth tore along the Loom-stitchers' seam, and then the rest went like a rope through a hand.

The Cut was not a war. It was nine jobs left undone in the same breath.

chapters.title: The March as rest
chapters.text:
The March is where the thread frayed thinnest and the fallen ground came to rest. Halls lie sunk to the lintel. Camps keep time with no one at the drum. Crystal grows where the Loom's tension still pools.

Walk it with a full Pulse cell and a steady hand. Ancestor Halls kept the tablets. Drum Circles kept the last beat. The Unsung is a keeper who went hollow waiting to be struck.

Everything here still answers a beat. That is not haunting. That is a world that never learned how to quit.

chapters.title: Holding is the work
chapters.text:
Mending is not a private miracle. Seat a Strand and your pad notices. Seat nine and the cut above your pad closes.

Read every tablet. Strike the Silent Drum when you are ready. Offer at hearths. Ask politely, smaller than the old world asked.

The world does not snap back. It learns to hold.

chapters.title: First camp
chapters.text:
Goal: store enough power to try your first workshop. Pulse is Tribal Power's stored energy.

You need
A Drumheart, a clear place to stand, and optionally a Pulse Cell. Use Recipes in this book, or JEI when it is installed, to follow any missing ingredients.

Steps
1. Place the Drumheart on your platform. Keep nearby machines within 8 blocks.
2. With an empty hand, right-click the drum about once a second. Steady beats add more Pulse than rapid clicking.
3. Keep playing until you have a reserve. Machines spend stored Pulse while they work, so one beat may not finish a recipe.
4. Use a Pulse Cell on the drum when you want to carry power for tools or travel. Leave power in the drum for your workshop.

Check
Inspect the drum: its stored Pulse should increase. You now have manual power, not an automatic supply.

If it does not work
Empty your hand. Wait between beats. Remove a redstone signal if the generator is paused. Read the current recipe in Recipes, or JEI when it is installed, if an ingredient differs from another guide.

chapters.title: Spirit Pulse
chapters.text:
Pulse is stored energy. A generator produces it; a machine spends it. A Pulse Cell carries it for tools and other uses.

Range
For your first workshop, put the generator beside the machine. Nearby power is checked within 8 blocks. Stored energy in a distant or unloaded generator cannot help.

Supply and demand
A machine can run briefly from a reserve even when it spends power faster than you generate it. If it repeatedly starts and stops, compare the required Pulse with your generation rate. Add generation or build a larger reserve.

Important
A carried Pulse Cell is not the same as a nearby powered generator. Matching totems provide an elemental requirement, called attunement; they do not automatically create power.

Check
Crouch and right-click a machine with the Spirit Codex. Read its power and attunement messages separately. Machines use generators first, then available totem buffers supplied by a Conductor. Each totem holds 250 Pulse.

chapters.title: Drumheart
chapters.text:
The Drumheart turns timed clicks or redstone pulses into stored Pulse. It holds 1,000 Pulse.

Steps
1. Place it beside the machine you want to supply.
2. Right-click with an empty hand about once a second. A well-timed beat gives 24 Pulse; an offbeat gives 10.
3. To automate it, use a Heartbeat plate set to one second and connect its output to the drum.
4. Use a Pulse Cell on the drum to carry some stored energy away.

Check
Stored Pulse should rise after each accepted beat, up to 1,000. A machine drawing power at the same time may keep the number low.

Timing details
Redstone beats 17 to 23 game ticks apart earn the larger amount. Beats less than 8 ticks apart are ignored. Twenty ticks is one second at normal server speed. Rapid clicking is less useful than a steady rhythm. Rank adds 15% Pulse a beat per rank, not the workshop 118%.

chapters.title: Ley Collector
chapters.text:
The Ley Collector makes Pulse from the landscape within 8 blocks. Open sky, water, plants and other camp signs raise its rate. A roof loses sky, rain and storm; it is weaker, not dead.

How:
1. Place the Ley Collector under open sky. It listens in an 8-block radius, the same as the lattice.
2. Each beat starts at 1. Open sky adds 1 by day or 3 at night; rain 2; thunder 1 more; water up to 4; plants up to 4; totem voices up to 3; a hearth 1; animals up to 2; The March 2; a full moon 1. Cap 16. A roof loses sky, rain and storm; water, plants, voices, a hearth and animals still add.
3. It adds Pulse every two seconds, and holds 2,000 Pulse. The Ley Lens total is that beat, not Pulse a second.
4. When the Lens beat is at least 8 of 16, nearby totems stay answered. How full the collector is does not pad them.
5. A redstone signal pauses generation. Rank it in Echo Attune, Bind, then Manifest for 15% Pulse a second per rank, not the workshop 118%. Sneak-use a Ley Lens on it to print the exact factor breakdown. Hold the lens to paint the ground in a 17-by-17.

chapters.title: Keeping
chapters.text:
Totems need occasional activity as well as available power. Their activity state is called Keeping.

The states
Answered means active: about 40 minutes of loaded time after a use. Dim means activity is fading: another 40 minutes, and matching stations take about 30% longer. Quiet means new work may pause. A full generator does not automatically wake a quiet totem.

Steps
1. Inspect a stopped station with the Codex. Check whether the problem is power or a quiet totem.
2. Interact with the totem or use a Bone Chime to wake it.
3. Keep using the matching workshop. Nearby players, Kin and a strong Ley Collector can help maintain activity.

Check
The totem should report an active state and the waiting machine should resume when its other requirements are met.

Planning a camp
Open sky, water and plants last twice as long. A roofed hole forgets you faster. A Heartbeat plate can keep a Drumheart producing power, but that alone does not maintain every totem's activity.

chapters.title: Pulse Resonator
chapters.text:
The Pulse Resonator makes Pulse automatically. It needs one reusable Echo catalyst and at least two different elemental totems nearby.

Steps
1. Make an Echo Shard in Echo Shatter using stone and an Earth totem.
2. Place the Resonator and right-click it with the shard. The catalyst stays inside.
3. Place Earth and Fire Resonance Totems within 8 blocks of the Resonator. Two Earth totems count as one element, not two.
4. Wait a second, then inspect the Resonator. Stored Pulse should rise.

Check
A shard and two distinct elements produce 6 Pulse a second. Pack generation settings do not change that base rate. Rank the Resonator itself for 15% Pulse a second per rank. The Resonator holds 2,500 Pulse. This may be slower than a workshop's consumption. Let energy build up, seat a stronger catalyst, or add more voices.

If it stays dark
Remove a pausing redstone signal. Check the catalyst and the two different elements. Only Answered totems count; Quiet voices do not (the Loom Anchor is different — quiet totems still count there). Crouch and right-click with the Codex for diagnostics. Crouch with an empty hand to remove the catalyst.

Later
Stronger catalysts improve output. Six elements require the Voice Ring layout; read its placement diagram before expanding. A heap still caps at five voices total, kinship included.

chapters.title: Harmonic ranks
chapters.text:
A catalyst is a reusable crystal you seat in the Resonator. Stronger crystals make more Pulse. None of them burn away.

How:
1. Rank 1 — Echo Shard: shatter stone, deepslate or March stone in Echo Shatter with an Earth totem.
2. Rank 2 — Attuned Echo: cook shards in Echo Attune with a Fire totem.
3. Rank 3 — Bound Echo: cook attuned echoes in Echo Bind with a Water totem.
4. Rank 4 — Resonant Core: cook Manifested Ingots in Echo Manifest with a Spirit totem.
5. Seat the crystal. Each second the Resonator makes (2 times distinct voices) plus (2 times rank). Two voices and a shard is 6 Pulse a second. Six voices in a Voice Ring and a Core is 20.

Kinship Totems add extra tribe voices. Sneak empty-handed to lift the crystal. Redstone pauses generation.

chapters.title: Carry the beat
chapters.text:
A Pulse Cell stores Pulse you can carry. Fill it from a Drumheart, a Resonator, or a voice-craft, then spend it on tools, rites and travel. A cell in your pocket is not a nearby generator — workshops still need Pulse within 8 blocks.

How:
1. Craft a Pulse Cell. Use it on a Drumheart (25 Pulse per use), a Resonator (100 Pulse per use), or a voice-craft such as a Wind Harp (100 Pulse per use) to fill the cell from that store. The generator loses the Pulse; the cell gains it. A Ley Collector does not fill a cell this way.
2. Ordinary cells hold 200 Pulse. Greater Cells hold 1,200.
3. Carry charged cells for spells, Spiritgear, charms, travel and tablet rites. A pocket cell is not in range for workshops or tablet rites.
4. A cell on a Gate Drum adds up to 25 Pulse per use into the drum; a cell on a gate keystone adds up to 100. Travel spends that store, not a cell in your pocket.
5. A Pulse Gauge pointed at a cell-holding machine reads how full it is.

chapters.title: Six voices
chapters.text:
Workshops need Pulse and a matching Resonance Totem within 8 blocks. The totem is an elemental requirement, not a generator. If the voice is missing, the station pauses and spends nothing.

How:
1. Craft the Resonance Totem of the voice you need.
2. Place it within 8 blocks of the station.
3. Earth: Shatter and the Stone Font. Fire: Attune and the Ember Kiln. Water: Bind. Spirit: Manifest. Air: motion and Song. Loom: Unweave and Far Gates.
4. Kinship Totems lend that tribe's element to nearby stations. On a Pulse Resonator they also add extra tribe voices, not a seventh element.
5. Crouch and right-click the Codex on a paused station: it names the missing voice.

chapters.title: Chalk and conductor
chapters.text:
The Lattice Conductor does not make Pulse. It pulls Pulse from nearby generators and pushes it into chalk-linked totem buffers.

How:
1. Place two or more Resonance Totems.
2. Right-click the first with Ritual Chalk, then the second (they must be within 16 blocks). You should see "Lattice link sealed".
3. Place a Lattice Conductor within 8 blocks of those totems.
4. Place a generator within 8 blocks of the Conductor: a Drumheart, Ley Collector, Pulse Resonator, or a voice-craft such as a Wind Harp, Wave Drum, Ember Horn, Loom Anchor or Wake Bell.
5. Every second it pulls up to 10 Pulse from nearby generators and pushes it into the linked totems. Each totem holds 250 Pulse. Ranked conductors pull more. Song Benches that need help are filled first.
6. Right-click the Conductor for a 25-Pulse burst and a status line.
7. Every two seconds, if the lattice holds Pulse, it moves Echo items between Song Benches and nearby Ancestral Caches.

A lever on the Conductor pauses it. "No network" means the totems are not chalk-linked. "No Pulse" means bring a generator closer. Ley Binding can also join distant totems as if they stood side by side.

chapters.title: Echo workshops
chapters.text:
Echo stations turn ingredients into new materials. Each recipe needs three things: the correct input, a matching elemental totem, and enough Pulse.

First layout
Place a generator beside Echo Shatter and an Earth Resonance Totem beside the station. All three can sit on the same floor. Put an output hopper below the station if you want automatic collection.

Steps
1. Open the station and place the ingredient in its input slot.
2. Read Recipes in this book, or JEI when it is installed, for the output, time and elemental requirement.
3. Charge the generator and keep the matching totem within 8 blocks.
4. Take the result from the output slots. Keep some output space free.

Automation
The side controls choose Input, Output, Both or Closed. By default, five faces accept items and the bottom exports them. For adjacent machines, set the source face to Output and the receiving face to Input. Hoppers follow the same settings.

If work stops
Check power, totem type, empty output space and redstone. A lever pauses work. The configured power multiplier changes machine cost, so use diagnostics for your current setup.

Ember Kiln
The Fire station smelts with Pulse instead of coal. Cobble becomes stone; grit becomes an ingot. Sit Echo Shatter on it, Output into Input, so grit walks down.

chapters.title: Shatter
chapters.text:
Echo Shatter has two different jobs: making Echo Shards from stone and crushing building materials or ores. Cobblestone does not make Echo Shards.

You need
Echo Shatter, an Earth Resonance Totem, stone or deepslate, and a charged generator within 8 blocks.

Steps
1. Place the generator and totem beside the station.
2. Smelt cobblestone into stone if you have no stone yet.
3. Put stone in the station's input slot. Keep its output slots empty.
4. Charge the generator until the recipe can finish. Take the Echo Shard from the output.

Check
An Echo Shard is the small reusable catalyst for your first Pulse Resonator. The shard recipe uses 16 Pulse per second before the configured multiplier. A reserve lets a slower generator complete a batch.

Other inputs
Cobblestone becomes gravel; gravel becomes sand. Sand becomes dust when the supported sieving mod is installed, or clay otherwise. Raw metals and supported ores become grit at 4 seconds and 20 Pulse a second before pack settings; sit Shatter on an Ember Kiln so grit walks into ingots. Gems: silk-touched ore shatters straight to the gem at twice the ore drop. Use Recipes in this book, or JEI when it is installed, for the exact input and output in this installation.

chapters.title: Attune and Bind
chapters.text:
Echo Attune (Fire) turns Echo Shards into Attuned Echoes. Echo Bind (Water) turns Attuned Echoes into Bound Echoes. Sit them Output-into-Input to chain without a hopper.

How:
1. Place Echo Attune with a Fire totem within 8. Feed Echo Shards. Take Attuned Echoes.
2. Place Echo Bind with a Water totem within 8. Feed Attuned Echoes. Take Bound Echoes.
3. Bind also turns wool into Spiritweave and dirt into clay.
4. Sit Attune on Bind, Output into Input, and the chain walks without a hopper.
5. Open Recipes in this book, or JEI when it is installed, for time and Pulse. A lever pauses either station.

chapters.title: Manifest
chapters.text:
Echo Manifest (Spirit) turns Bound Echoes into Manifested Ingots, then ingots into Resonant Cores.

How:
1. Place Echo Manifest. Spirit totem within 8.
2. Feed Bound Echoes. Take Manifested Ingots.
3. Feed Manifested Ingots. Take Resonant Cores.
4. Cores unlock Greater Cells, Spiritgear, long-distance automation and gate keystones.
5. Sit Bind on Manifest, Output into Input, and the chain walks without a hopper.

Open Recipes in this book, or JEI when it is installed, for time and Pulse. A lever pauses the station.

chapters.title: Ember Kiln
chapters.text:
The Ember Kiln smelts with Pulse instead of coal. It needs a Fire Resonance Totem within 8. Grit becomes an ingot; cobble becomes stone, the same as a furnace.

How:
1. Place the Kiln. Fire totem within 8.
2. Sit Echo Shatter on it, Output into Input, so grit walks down.
3. Feed grit for an ingot, or any furnace input for that furnace result. Cobble becomes stone, not an ingot.
4. Each furnace smelt is 10 seconds and 32 Pulse a second before pack settings. The default 2.0 consumption multiplier doubles that. A lever pauses it.
5. Rank it in Echo Attune, Bind, then Manifest like any other workshop.

chapters.title: Echo Unweave
chapters.text:
Echo Unweave (Loom) reverses the lattice. Missing Loom pauses and spends nothing.

How:
1. Place Echo Unweave. Loom Resonance Totem within 8.
2. Feed a Manifested Ingot for 2 Bound Echoes, a Resonant Core for 3 Manifested Ingots, Spiritweave for wool, or damaged Spiritgear for one Manifested Ingot.
3. Fresh undamaged tools refuse Unweave.
4. Sit Bind or Manifest Output into this station if you want a reverse chain without a hopper.
5. Rank it in Echo Attune, Bind, then Manifest. A lever pauses insert and work.

chapters.title: Song Bench
chapters.text:
A Song Bench crafts one Echo-stage item at a time. Dedicated Echo stations (Shatter, Attune, Bind, Manifest, Kiln, Unweave) cost much less Pulse and are better for batches.

How:
1. Place a Song Bench. Matching totem within 8.
2. Insert one Echo-stage ingredient (stone for a shard, not cobble).
3. Click empty-handed to sing. Sneak-click to take the item back.
4. Shatter spends 8 Pulse a tick for 2 seconds. Attune 10 a tick for 3 seconds. Bind 12 a tick for 4 seconds. Manifest 16 a tick for 5 seconds. Dedicated stations use written recipes and cost much less.
5. Rank it in Echo Attune, Bind, then Manifest: the song shortens, Pulse per tick rises, Pulse per craft stays about even.

chapters.title: Ancestral Cache
chapters.text:
A local 54-slot inventory for camp supplies.

How:
1. Place it beside or under a station.
2. Open it. The IO pad sets each face to Input, Output, Both or Closed; sneak-empty-hand on a face does the same.
3. Set the touching faces to Output into Input and the cache feeds or drains the station with no hopper and no relay. Both-into-Both does nothing, so stacks cannot ping-pong.
4. Hoppers and pipes still honour those faces. Relays are for distance.
5. A lever locks access and automation. A comparator reads how full it is.

chapters.title: Deep Cache
chapters.text:
A personal 54-slot vault shared between every Deep Cache you place.

How:
1. Place a Deep Cache.
2. Visiting The March attunes you; otherwise opening costs 5 Pulse.
3. A Wayfarer Satchel opens the same personal vault.
4. Sneak-use the satchel to switch between your vault and a shared camp vault.
5. A lever locks the block. The vault itself is not emptied by a pause.

chapters.title: Spirit Cistern
chapters.text:
The camp tank. One fluid, 16,000 mB (16 buckets), and the fluid stays on the dropped item.

How:
1. Place the cistern. Right-click with a bucket to fill or empty it. Empty-handed click reads mB.
2. Standard fluid pipes, a Tide Pump, or a fluid relay can fill and drain it. Relays and the Tide Pump move fluid; they are not tanks.
3. A held redstone signal locks filling and draining, including remote relays. Stored fluid stays.
4. A comparator facing away reads fullness: 0 empty, then 1 to 15 as it fills.
5. Break it: the dropped cistern keeps the fluid. Place it again and the tank is still full. A Wave Drum also keeps its internal water tank. Relays and the Tide Pump move fluid; they are not tanks.

Spring Calling can mark a placed cistern a spring so it refills itself. Moving the block ends the spring; water already inside still rides on the item.

chapters.title: Wireless cargo
chapters.text:
Snap a relay plate onto any face of a machine. Relays are for distance; hoppers and matching Output-into-Input faces are for neighbours.

How:
1. Snap a Local, Longreach or Astral relay onto a face.
2. Seat the same item in both Bond slots to pair them.
3. Sneak-click a plate to switch extract or insert.
4. Water Seal in the Rune slot moves fluid, Earth Seal moves items; empty uses the plate's name.
5. The Lattice Tuner still marks a destination face, then links one plate. Hoppers cannot steal the Bond or Rune. For fluid, park a Spirit Cistern at each end — relays move fluid, they do not store it.

chapters.title: Cargo tiers
chapters.text:
Three distances. Rank the plate in Echo Attune, Bind, then Manifest to move more — and pay more Pulse.

How:
1. Local relays reach 32 blocks. Cost 4 Pulse per successful beat before pack settings.
2. Longreach relays reach 128. Cost 8 before pack settings.
3. Astral relays have no distance limit and can cross dimensions. Cost 16 before pack settings.
4. The default 2.0 consumption multiplier doubles those costs. Rank 1/2/3 then pays 118% / 143% / 182% of the scaled cost and moves that much more cargo (about 19 / 23 / 29 items, or 294 / 357 / 455 mB).
5. Leave both ends loaded. Unloaded destinations pause; they do not void.

chapters.title: Cargo rhythm
chapters.text:
Each second, a relay moves up to 16 items or 250 mB.

How:
1. Pair the plates. Keep Pulse within 8 of the source plate.
2. Both ends must already be loaded.
3. Unloaded or full destinations pause safely.
4. Relays never keep distant chunks loaded themselves — put a Wayanchor at the far end if it must keep working while you travel.
5. Ranked plates move more per beat and spend more Pulse, so Pulse per item stays about even.

chapters.title: Cargo controls
chapters.text:
A constant redstone signal pauses the plate. A comparator tells you why.

How:
1. Power the plate with redstone to pause it.
2. Comparator: 0 unlinked, 1 linked but waiting, 15 transferring.
3. Lock the receiver with redstone when you need a remote stop.
4. A tuner-bound destination survives pickup. Bond and Rune drop beside the plate.
5. Sneak-click to flip extract and insert without breaking the pair.

chapters.title: Pulse to FE
chapters.text:
The Pulse Adapter converts Pulse into Forge Energy (FE) for other mods' machines.

How:
1. Place the Adapter beside a generator and an FE machine.
2. It converts 1 Pulse into 100 FE, up to 20 Pulse each second. Ranked adapters convert more Pulse, and more FE, in the same second.
3. It buffers 16,000 FE and exports to standard energy receivers. It cannot receive FE.
4. Redstone stops conversion and extraction.
5. A comparator reads the FE buffer.

chapters.title: Waystone paths
chapters.text:
A compass stores a landing block. Use it to spend Pulse from a carried cell and return there.

How:
1. Sneak-use a compass on the top of a solid floor to bind a landing.
2. Use it to return. Keep two clear dry blocks above the floor.
3. Power the landing floor with redstone to lock arrival.
4. Travel spends Pulse from a carried cell. A 5-second cooldown follows.
5. If there is nowhere to stand, the trip refuses and spends nothing. Pulse is taken only after the floor is clear and dry.

chapters.title: Travel tiers
chapters.text:
Three distances, one cooldown.

How:
1. Waystone Compass: 128 blocks, same world, 20 Pulse.
2. Horizon Compass: any distance in one world, 40 Pulse.
3. Astral Compass: across dimensions, 100 Pulse.
4. Bind a landing before you go. Keep two clear dry blocks above it.
5. Travel has a 5-second cooldown. Redstone on the landing floor locks arrival.

chapters.title: The March
chapters.text:
The Gate Drum is a charged portal, not a Drumheart. Fill it with Pulse, then empty-handed use it to walk through. March materials unlock Astral transport, the Loom voice, and the last of the tablets.

How:
1. Charge Pulse Cells. Bind a return compass to a dry floor at home.
2. Place a Gate Drum. A Pulse Cell adds up to 25 Pulse each use; sneak empty-handed adds 5. The drum holds 200. Empty-handed use spends 20 stored Pulse and walks you through. Redstone locks the drum. A blocked landing refunds that 20. A Way Gate pair is the later bulk route.
3. Read every tablet in Ancestor Halls. The Codex records them.
4. Strike a Silent Drum four beats, a breath apart, when you are ready for The Unsung.
5. Bring March Crystal, Loom Thread and an Unsung Heart home. They open the sixth voice.

chapters.title: Sixfold Staff
chapters.text:
Crouch and right-click to choose a voice, then right-click to cast. The staff spends Pulse from a carried cell, not durability.

How:
1. Craft the staff. Carry a charged Pulse Cell.
2. Sneak-use to cycle Earth, Fire, Water, Air, Spirit, Loom.
3. Use to cast. Earth slows foes. Fire strikes and ignites for 4 seconds. Water heals and cleanses. Air grants a short leap and slow falling. Spirit reveals enemies within 12 blocks. Loom tethers a foe up to 8 blocks toward you or, sneaking with no target, stitches you 6 blocks forward.
4. Offensive spells reach 18 blocks, target hostiles, and stop at solid obstacles.
5. Water rests 8 seconds; other voices rest 2. Stitch rests 1.5 seconds.

chapters.title: Staff costs
chapters.text:
The staff spends Pulse, not durability.

How:
1. Earth 12, Fire 18, Water 24, Air 16, Spirit 20 Pulse.
2. Loom 6 to tether (up to 8 blocks), 10 to stitch (6 blocks).
3. Keep a cell in your inventory. The staff drinks from it.
4. If the cell is dry, the cast does not fire.
5. Water rests for 8 seconds; other voices for 2. Stitch rests 1.5 seconds. Offensive spells reach 18 blocks.

chapters.title: Resonance Maul
chapters.text:
A 3-by-3 plane of stone, paid in Pulse.

How:
1. Hold the maul in your main hand.
2. Sneak-use a stone face to excavate a 3-by-3 plane.
3. Each block costs 8 Pulse.
4. Tool requirements and normal player block protection still apply.
5. If Pulse runs out mid-swing, remaining blocks stay. The maul then rests one second.

chapters.title: Spiritweave
chapters.text:
Spiritweave armor spends Pulse from a carried cell. Sneak-use a piece on a placed Resonance Totem to replace its default boon with that voice.

How:
1. Craft Spiritweave armor. Fresh pieces are diamond-hard, rank 0.
2. Unlinked hood: night sight. Robe: resistance. Leggings: speed. Boots: slow falling when descending.
3. Unlinked pieces spend 2 Pulse every four seconds from a carried cell.
4. Sneak-use a piece on a placed Resonance Totem with 40 Pulse to bind a voice (3 Pulse upkeep). The bound voice replaces the default boon.
5. Rank the cloth in Echo Attune, Bind, then Manifest. Air boots only spend Pulse when Slow Falling is not already on you.

chapters.title: Spiritgear ranks
chapters.text:
The Echo stations teach cloth and iron the same three voices they taught the catalysts.

How:
1. Craft Spiritgear or Spiritweave. Fresh pieces are diamond-hard, rank 0, 1024 durability.
2. Seat a piece in Echo Attune (Fire totem) to raise rank 0 to 1: 8 seconds and 24 Pulse a second before pack settings.
3. Seat it in Echo Bind (Water) for 1 to 2: 10 seconds and 32 Pulse a second. Bind refuses rank 0.
4. Seat it in Echo Manifest (Spirit) for 2 to 3: 12 seconds and 40 Pulse a second. You cannot skip.
5. Rank 1 cheapens action Pulse by one: mining costs 2, a hit costs 3, a use costs 1 (floor 1). Rank 2 skips the extra hurt when starved. Rank 3 mines at netherite speed and often spares the edge even without Pulse. A Loom-linked pick already spends 0 Pulse to mine.

Unweave of a damaged tool still returns one Manifested Ingot and forgets rank and voice.

chapters.title: Totem-bound gear
chapters.text:
Sneak-use a piece on a placed Resonance Totem with 40 Pulse. The totem is not consumed; overwrite is allowed.

How:
1. Place the totem. Carry a charged cell.
2. Sneak-use the tool or armor on it. The action bar names the voice.
3. Mixed sets are intended. The bound voice replaces the default armor boon.
4. Earth picks open 3-by-3 stone; Fire smelts; Water silks; Air hastes; Spirit glints ores; Loom mines without Pulse.
5. Loom needs a Loom totem. Armor: Earth hood turns aside one projectile in five (about one in three at rank 3). Fire robe ignites attackers for 3 seconds. Spirit robe makes attackers glow. Water robe regenerates (longer at rank 3). Air robe ignores knockback. Earth boots cut knockback and do not trample farmland. Spirit boots cancel fall (rank 3 bounce from a high drop). Loom boots sneak-stitch 4 blocks, or 6 at rank 3, then rest 8 seconds. Extra 3-by-3 blocks spend Pulse the same way as the first.

chapters.title: Machine ranks
chapters.text:
Workshops learn the same three voices, at twice Spiritgear's station cost: Attune 16s/48 Pulse a second, Bind 20s/64, Manifest 24s/80.

How:
1. Pick up the machine. Seat the item in Echo Attune (Fire), then Bind (Water), then Manifest (Spirit).
2. Rank 1 runs at 85% time and draws 118% Pulse. Rank 2 at 70% time and 143% Pulse. Rank 3 at 55% time and 182% Pulse.
3. Pulse per craft stays about even — the extra speed is paid on the lattice. Ranked generators add 15% Pulse a second per rank, not the workshop 118%. Relays move more, and pay more Pulse for the extra cargo. Camp hands beat faster at the same Pulse per move.
4. Place it again. The rank rides on the block and on the item when you pick it up.

chapters.title: Spirit Charms
chapters.text:
Worn seals. Three slots that Tribal Power owns — no other mod is required.

How:
1. Craft a charm. Use it to wear it; sneak-use to open the three slots.
2. Sky is creative flight. Ember is fire. Tide is breath and swim. Root is resistance. Lantern is sight. Spindle is luck, and about three times in ten it refunds up to 2 Pulse into a carried cell every two seconds. Ward turns aside about one projectile in four, or one in two if Spirit is also on the charm. Hearth keeps you fed. Veil hides you while you sneak.
3. Chorus starts silent. Sneak-use it on a Ritual Brazier with three different totems within 8 and 200 Pulse to bind every nearby voice. Extra sneak-uses on totems add voices for 40 Pulse each.
4. Worn cost is 2 Pulse per voice every two seconds. A silent Chorus still costs 2. Unequip if the drum runs dry.

chapters.title: Ritual Brazier
chapters.text:
Seat a reusable elemental seal. With its matching totem and Pulse nearby, the brazier sustains a blessing.

How:
1. Place the brazier. Place the matching totem within 8.
2. Seat the seal. It is not consumed.
3. Keep Pulse nearby. It spends 8 Pulse every two seconds for players within 6 blocks.
4. A lever pauses it. Sneak empty-handed to recover the seal.
5. Tablet rites want a circle of pedestals around this brazier — see Draw the circle.

chapters.title: Camp blessings
chapters.text:
Earth grants haste; Fire resists flame; Water regenerates; Air slows falls; Spirit grants night sight; Loom grants luck and threads 2 Pulse into a carried cell each beat.

How:
1. Seat the matching seal in a Ritual Brazier.
2. Place that voice's totem within 8.
3. Stand within 6 blocks. The blessing ticks while Pulse lasts.
4. Redstone pauses the brazier. Stored Pulse is not dumped.
5. Sneak empty-handed to recover the seal.

chapters.title: Redstone language
chapters.text:
A constant redstone signal pauses machines. A short pulse (a rising edge) triggers devices that do one thing, such as a Drumheart beat.

How:
1. Hold a line high to pause workshops, conductors, resonators, collectors, relays, braziers, meshes, fonts, pedestals, gate keystones and every generator, and to lock storage and travel destinations.
2. A rising edge is a call. Only devices that do a discrete thing listen: a Drumheart takes a beat, a Ritual Brazier fires its seated rite, a keystone lights or darkens.
3. Song Thread carries 0 to 15 weakly, like dust — it will not latch on stone.
4. Song plates output from the facing. Unary plates read the back; binary plates read left and right.
5. Nothing is ever lost to a pause.

chapters.title: Read the camp
chapters.text:
Comparators tell you what a machine is holding without opening it.

How:
1. Put a comparator against the block, facing away from it.
2. They read stored Pulse, inventory or fluid fullness, FE buffer, and relay activity.
3. A pause keeps stored resources intact.
4. Use clocks, levers and comparators to choreograph the camp.
5. Crouch and right-click the Codex if the number is not enough and you want a sentence.

chapters.title: Other workshops
chapters.text:
Lattice recipes use the normal recipe manager and sync to clients.

How:
1. Open Recipes in this book, or JEI when it is installed. Every Echo station lists time, Pulse and voice.
2. Datapacks can add tribalpower:lattice recipes using shared ingredient tags.
3. Missing voices pause work. Full output pauses work. A lever pauses insert and work.
4. Sit stations Output-into-Input to walk a chain without hoppers.
5. Relays are for distance.

chapters.title: The veil at night
chapters.text:
After dusk, the sky unfolds in slow curtains of green and violet.

How:
1. Wait for night in the Overworld. The March carries a colder sky.
2. Rain veils the aurora.
3. Client settings can reduce its detail or disable it for shader packs.
4. It is the sky trying to remember a schedule. It does not give Pulse by itself — a Ley Collector under that sky does.

chapters.title: Gentle harvesting
chapters.text:
Brush adult Dawn Stags, Lantern Foxes and Mossbacks for renewable reagents.

How:
1. Find an adult. Young animals do not yield materials.
2. Use an empty hand to brush. Each rests for one minute between harvests.
3. Breed with wheat (stag), sweet berries (fox) and seagrass (mossback).
4. Bond an adult with a Bonding Charm to double the reagent and keep a companion.
5. Use Recipes in this book, or JEI when it is installed, to follow the reagent into your workshop.

chapters.title: Broken guardians
chapters.text:
Ashbound, Rootbound and Reed Stalkers haunt forests and marshes in the Overworld. All can also be found in the March.

How:
1. Build lighted paths. Hostile creatures require darkness.
2. Keep water close to Ashbound. Rootbound roots you; wait it out. Reed Stalkers poison — milk or distance.
3. Their reagents attune into two Attuned Echoes under Spirit.
4. A Hush Totem or Still Night keeps a camp from growing a new pack overnight.
5. Field notes live on each creature's own page.

chapters.title: Beyond the Gate
chapters.text:
The March biomes keep different remnants. Bind a return compass and carry charged Pulse cells before you step through a Gate Drum.

How:
1. Steppe: Dawn Stags and rabbits graze. Ashbound, Rootbound, Rift Hounds and Echo Weavers hunt. Ancestor Halls sink to the lintel.
2. Highlands: Drum Circles and The Unsung. Hollow Sentinels, Storm Moths, Cinder Imps and Rift Hounds.
3. Crystal Fields: the Loom-stitcher Crystal Spire. Lantern Foxes, Shardbacks, Mourning Bells, Reed Stalkers and Echo Weavers.
4. Snow Fields: Lantern Foxes, rabbits and polar bears on freeze turf. Ember Wastes: sparse fire country — walkers and wisps, no grazing herds. Reed Fen: frogs, fish, glow squid and Reed Stalkers in the wet.
5. Sneak-use this book on anything silent. Creature field notes live on each bestiary page.

chapters.title: Answering a spell
chapters.text:
Storm Moths, Cinder Imps and Mourning Bells gather visible motes before casting.

How:
1. Watch for the gathering. That is your warning.
2. Step behind solid cover to interrupt. The spell never burns or replaces terrain.
3. A charged staff is useful for keeping distance.
4. Sneak against The Unsung's shockwave; that is a different fight, on its own page.
5. Their reagents bind or attune like any other remnant.

chapters.title: Returning the song
chapters.text:
Bring creature reagents to the Echo workshops.

How:
1. Gentle animal harvests, Storm Wings and Echo Silk bind into Spiritweave under Water.
2. Other hostile remnants attune into two Attuned Echoes under Spirit.
3. Existing recipes remain available. Open Recipes in this book, or JEI when it is installed.
4. Rootbinders favour Mossback Scale. Colony-keepers favour Lantern Down. Offer what you brush.
5. A bonded familiar sheds double, once a minute.

chapters.title: Wayanchor
chapters.text:
Sustain the chunk containing the anchor for 16 Pulse each second.

How:
1. Place the anchor in the chunk that must stay loaded — a distant relay endpoint, a pit, a gate.
2. Keep Pulse nearby. A 2,400-Pulse reserve bridges interruptions; nearby generators refill up to 80 Pulse a second.
3. The anchor holds one chunk, not a radius. Up to 32 anchors may run per dimension (twelve if you share a camp).
4. Redstone or an empty reserve releases its ticket. Removing the block releases it immediately.
5. Place another at the other end of a relay if both ends must keep working while you travel.

chapters.title: Hush Totem
chapters.text:
A quiet circle suppresses hostile spawning within 24 blocks for 8 Pulse per second.

How:
1. Place the totem in the middle of camp.
2. Keep Pulse nearby. A 2,400-Pulse reserve bridges interruptions; nearby generators refill up to 80 Pulse a second. It covers natural and spawner-born hostiles, including Summoning Cradles.
3. It does not remove existing mobs, stop animals, or override commands and spawn eggs.
4. Redstone silences the ward immediately.
5. Keep a cradle outside the circle, or use redstone to alternate between peace and summoning.

chapters.title: Grove Tender
chapters.text:
The Grove Tender keeps a living bed.

How:
1. Place it yourself at crop height in the middle of a 9-by-9 plot so it is claimed. An unclaimed tender will not tend.
2. Hopper seeds, saplings, cane, berries, nether wart or cocoa beans into the top row.
3. Keep Pulse nearby: 4 to plant, 12 to harvest, 16 to urge a sapling, stem, crop or berry bush to grow.
4. Pull harvests from below. Full output leaves the plant standing.
5. A lever pauses work and inventory.

It plants and harvests wheat-family crops, nether wart, cocoa, sweet berries, sugar cane, cactus and bamboo, then takes logs and leaves in a 9-wide, 11-tall column. One job each second. Player protection still applies.

chapters.title: Binding Effigy
chapters.text:
An empty or exhausted effigy remembers a living spirit without harming it.

How:
1. Craft an empty Binding Effigy.
2. Sneak-use it on an eligible animal or hostile creature.
3. Common farm animals, zombies, skeletons, spiders, creepers and the thirteen Tribal Power creatures can be imprinted. Bosses cannot.
4. A live binding cannot be overwritten.
5. An imprint alone has no summons: awaken it through the Three-voice Binding.

chapters.title: Three-voice Binding
chapters.text:
The recipe is deliberately a ritual, not a spawn-egg shortcut.

How:
1. Seat a Spirit Seal in a Ritual Brazier.
2. Place Earth, Air and Spirit Totems within eight blocks.
3. Supply 200 nearby Pulse and carry three Spiritweave.
4. Use your imprinted, exhausted effigy on the brazier with redstone off. The three voices knot 512 summoning threads into it.
5. Renew an exhausted effigy the same way, or first imprint another eligible spirit.

chapters.title: Summoning Cradle
chapters.text:
Place a bound effigy in the first slot and Spiritweave in the second.

How:
1. Every ten seconds the cradle attempts one summon on a clear, dry floor within three blocks.
2. A successful summon costs 80 Pulse, one Spiritweave and one bound thread.
3. Eight nearby mobs within twelve blocks pause it. Hostiles cannot be called in Peaceful or inside a Hush ward.
4. Failed or blocked attempts spend nothing. A comparator reads remaining threads. Redstone pauses everything.
5. Bottom automation can retrieve an exhausted effigy for renewal. Picking up the cradle drops the same effigy with its remaining count intact.

chapters.title: Spirit Lantern
chapters.text:
A carved copper-and-wood lantern brightens the camp at light level 15 without fuel.

How:
1. Place it along paths between workshops.
2. Redstone dims it.
3. A comparator reports whether it is lit.
4. Its animated crystal shares the living-lattice palette.
5. No Pulse is needed. Glow Reed, Shard Lamp, Echo Sconce and Ember Bowl are Pulse lights — they draw from the lattice instead.

chapters.title: Pulse lights
chapters.text:
Camp lamps that draw a trickle of Pulse. They have no buffer: nearby generators or they go dark.

How:
1. Craft Glow Reed, Shard Lamp or Echo Sconce (1 Pulse a second) or Ember Bowl (2 Pulse a second).
2. Place them within 8 of a generator. They light when they can pay, and go dark when they cannot.
3. Hang an Echo Sconce on a sturdy wall; it pops if the wall is gone.
4. A lever or redstone signal dims them immediately. A comparator reads 15 while lit, 0 when dark.
5. Spirit Lanterns still light with no Pulse. These four do not. A Wind Charm hangs from a sturdy ceiling, has no collision, and pops without a ceiling — it spends no Pulse.

Recipes in this book, or JEI when it is installed, list each lamp.

chapters.title: Wind Charm
chapters.text:
A hanging decoration. It spends no Pulse.

How:
1. Place it under a sturdy ceiling. It hangs in the air cell below.
2. You can walk through it: it has no collision.
3. Break the ceiling or the block above and it pops.
4. Redstone does nothing. It is not a Pulse light and not a Wind Harp.
5. Use Recipes in this book, or JEI when it is installed, for the craft.

chapters.title: Rain Chime
chapters.text:
The Rain Chime reports world weather as a comparator signal. It does not make Pulse. A roof does not mute it.

How:
1. Place the chime where a comparator can read it.
2. It sounds softly every ten seconds during rain.
3. Comparator: 8 for rain, 15 for thunder, 0 for clear skies.
4. Redstone mutes it and sets its output to zero.
5. Use the weather signal to choreograph Ley collection and camp lights. No fuel is needed.

chapters.title: Offering Table
chapters.text:
The Offering Table is a 27-slot camp store. Standing and favoured offerings go on the Tribe Hearth, not this table.

How:
1. Place it beside a hearth or a cradle for storage, not as a substitute hearth.
2. Hoppers and item pipes can insert or extract from every side.
3. A comparator reads fullness.
4. Redstone locks both the menu and automation.
5. No Pulse is needed for storage.

chapters.title: The sixth voice
chapters.text:
The sixth voice is the thread itself. Loom Thread comes from Ancestor Halls and The Unsung.

How:
1. Loot an Ancestor Hall for Loom Thread. Read the tablets.
2. Wake The Unsung for an Unsung Heart.
3. Craft the Loom totem: Unsung Heart, two threads, four March Crystals and two March Planks.
4. Echo Unweave reverses the lattice: a Manifested Ingot into 2 Bound Echoes, a Resonant Core into 3 Manifested Ingots, Spiritweave into wool, and damaged Spiritgear into one Manifested Ingot. Fresh undamaged tools refuse.
5. A Loom Seal in a Brazier threads 2 Pulse into carried cells every 2 seconds with Luck. The Sixfold Staff gains Tether and, sneaking with no target, Stitch.

chapters.title: Bonded spirits
chapters.text:
A companion that follows, waits, and sheds double reagent.

How:
1. Craft a Bonding Charm from two Spiritweave, a Spirit Shard and a creature reagent of the species you want.
2. Sneak-use a Ley Lens on a wild adult first. Frame, Stride, Fang, Hum and Keep each roll 0 to 3, so two foxes from the same clearing are not clones. The charm does not reroll.
3. Use the charm on an adult. Gentle animals: three tries in five, charm kept on failure. Remnants: two tries in five, charm spent on failure, and Voice standing with their tribe.
4. It follows within ten blocks, teleports to you past twelve, never despawns, and ignores your blows. Quiet Thread follows from eight and stops at two. Sneak-use it to wait or follow again. One fighter and two helpers may follow; sitters do not count.
5. Breed two of the same species for better threads. Marks are named quirks; some need both parents. Cloning Frame and Fang three times under one owner Frays Hum.

chapters.title: Lantern Fox familiar
chapters.text:
A bonded Lantern Fox lights the way.

How:
1. Bond an adult fox with a charm that includes Lantern Down.
2. An invisible Spirit Light travels with it. Glow-vein raises that light from 10 to 12.
3. Night Vision while you stay within eight blocks.
4. Every four seconds it marks ores within six blocks of itself with glints only you can see. Keen shortens that wait. Hum and night change the tempo.
5. Colony-keepers favour Lantern Down at the hearth.

chapters.title: Mossback and Dawn Stag familiars
chapters.text:
A bonded Mossback carries items. A bonded Dawn Stag can be ridden without a saddle.

How:
1. Bond an adult Mossback: sneak-use with an empty hand for a nine-slot saddlebag; sneak-use holding an item to make it wait or follow. It drops the bag on death.
2. Bond an adult Dawn Stag: use it to mount, no saddle. Steer with your gaze, hold jump for a short leap, sneak to dismount. It carries only the one it is bonded to.
3. Rootbinders favour Mossback Scale.
4. Brush either for double reagent.
5. Young animals cannot be bonded.

chapters.title: Hostile bonds
chapters.text:
Six remnants will walk with you if their tribe knows your name.

How:
1. Reach Voice (800) with that remnant's tribe: Grit-singers for a Shardback, Edge-walkers for a Rift Hound, Drumhearts for a Cinder Imp, Pattern-weavers for a Storm Moth, Seal-carvers for a Mourning Bell, Loom-stitchers for an Echo Weaver.
2. Craft a Bonding Charm with that remnant's reagent: Prism Carapace, Rift Tooth, Cinder Knot, Storm Wing, Bell Fragment or Echo Silk.
3. Use it on an adult. Two tries in five succeed. A failed charm is spent. The lattice does not reroll.
4. Ashbound, Rootbound, Reed Stalkers and Hollow Sentinels never answer.
5. Bonded remnants follow, wait, never despawn, ignore your blows, and shed double reagent when brushed. Feed them their reagent to breed; the child is not bonded.

chapters.title: Combat and company
chapters.text:
One fighter may follow. Two helpers may follow. Sitters do not count.

How:
1. Shardback and Rift Hound are combat: they strike who struck you, and who you strike. They still lose to guardians. Soft Maw (two copies) will not bite villagers or golems. Track (two copies, hounds) glints the last foe that hurt you.
2. A sitting Storm Moth leaves an invisible click of redstone 15 once a second. Click-true holds the pulse two extra ticks. It is not a drum.
3. A following Cinder Imp refunds 4 Pulse only while you hand-drum a Drumheart within eight blocks. Redstone beats get nothing. Tempo (two copies) refunds 2 more, 6 in all.
4. A Mourning Bell within eight blocks clears poison, weakness, hunger, mining fatigue, blindness and nausea. Still (two copies) also clears slowness. It never lifts Wither.
5. An Echo Weaver picks drops within 4 blocks into a five-slot pouch and tosses them to you. Gather (two copies) reaches 8. Sneak-use empty-handed to empty the pouch.

chapters.title: Shared camps
chapters.text:
A named camp with one vault, shared devices and pooled standing.

How:
1. /tribalpower camp create <name>. You become its first member.
2. Invite with /tribalpower camp invite <player> or a Camp Charter (paper, Spiritweave, Spirit Shard). Accept with /tribalpower camp join <name>. Invitations last five minutes.
3. Open any Deep Cache or Wayfarer Satchel; sneak-use switches between your personal vault and the shared 54-slot camp vault.
4. Members count as owners of each other's camp devices. The camp shares twelve Wayanchors per dimension instead of thirty-two each.
5. A quarter of every member's tribe standing lands on the camp. Leave, kick, rename and info complete the command.

chapters.title: World rites
chapters.text:
Carve a Rite Tablet from two stone, a creature reagent and the matching seal; the seal is handed back.

How:
1. Sneak-use the tablet on a Ritual Brazier holding that seal, inside its circle.
2. The brazier draws the rite's Pulse from the lattice within 8 blocks. If there is not enough, nothing is spent.
3. Rain Calling (Water, 400) brings twenty minutes of rain.
4. Sky Clearing (Air, 400) clears forty minutes.
5. Dawn Calling (Fire, 800) hurries the night to sunrise unless the game rule tribalpower:allowDawnRite is off.

chapters.title: Land rites
chapters.text:
Tablet rites change a region: faster crops, fewer hostiles, or a temporary totem link. Draw the circle first. Missing pedestals fail the cast without spending the tablet.

How:
1. Green Blessing (Earth, 600) blesses the nine chunks around the brazier for twenty minutes: crops, saplings and stems there take extra random ticks and sparkle green.
2. Still Night (Spirit, 600) hushes hostile spawning within 64 blocks for fifteen minutes, like a wide Hush Totem. Seal-carvers sell this tablet to Friends.
3. Ley Binding (Loom, 1,200) ties the brazier's nearest Resonance Totem to another within 64 blocks for thirty minutes.
4. A Conductor routes Pulse along the humming thread as if the totems stood side by side.
5. Draw the circle first. Missing pedestals fail the cast without spending the tablet.

chapters.title: Ley Lens
chapters.text:
A glass pane, a Copper Resonator and a Spirit Shard make a lens for ley sight.

How:
1. Hold it in either hand and use it to cycle four sights: ley strength on the ground (blue quiet, gold singing), the Pulse zone, nearby totem voices, and Tribal machines.
2. Each beat starts at 1. Open sky adds 1 by day or 3 at night; rain 2; thunder 1 more; water up to 4; plants up to 4; totem voices up to 3; a hearth 1; animals up to 2; The March 2; a full moon 1. Cap 16. The collector surveys 8 blocks; the lens paints 17 by 17.
3. Sneak-use the lens on a Ley Collector to print that collector's exact factor breakdown, or on a lattice animal or remnant to print its threads and Marks. The charm does not change those rolls.
4. Voice mode tints totems gold when answered, dull when dim, grey when quiet.
5. A roof loses sky, rain and storm; the collector is weaker, not dead. Water, plants, voices, a hearth and animals still add. A Lens beat of 8 or more (half of 16) pads nearby totems. Stored Pulse in the collector is not the pad.

chapters.title: Pulse logic
chapters.text:
The Pulse Gauge and Pulse Threshold turn stored Pulse into redstone. Song Thread and song plates carry that signal the way dust carries vanilla redstone, in all six directions.

How:
1. Point a Pulse Gauge at a Drumheart, Resonator or cell-holding machine. It emits 0 to 15 from every face except the arrow.
2. Point a Pulse Threshold the same way. Empty-handed use cycles 25, 50, 75, 100 percent. It emits while stored Pulse is at or above that percent, so a direct wire pauses a machine when Pulse is high. Put an Inverse plate on the line if you want the machine to pause when Pulse is too low.
3. Run Song Thread between plates. Power decays by one per block, in all six directions.
4. Snap a song plate onto a face. The facing is the output. Left and right are the two inputs; the back is the unary input.
5. Sneak-use Heartbeat, Drift or Tally plates to change their timing.

chapters.title: Codex diagnostics
chapters.text:
Sneak-use the Spirit Codex on any Tribal block to hear it explain itself.

How:
1. Sneak-use this book on the silent block.
2. It names stored Pulse, every generator within 8 blocks with its output this second, the attunements present, the Pulse it could draw, and whether redstone pauses it.
3. Workshops name their recipe and any missing voice or full output.
4. Relays report unloaded or locked endpoints. Braziers list the rites their seal allows.
5. Pattern anchors also show ghosts of missing pieces.

chapters.title: Standing
chapters.text:
Nine tribes kept the Loom, one Strand each; their camps still keep time.

How:
1. Find a camp: hearth, banner, four Kin.
2. Offer a favoured item at the Tribe Hearth for +3, the tribe's reagent for +8, any food for +1, or a charged Pulse Cell for +2 per 10 Pulse (at most 40 Pulse, +8). One hearth grants at most 60 standing a day from offerings.
3. Hostile kills within 24 blocks of a hearth give +1, twenty per day per tribe. A trade gives +2.
4. Ranks: Guest 50, Friend 150, Kin 400, Voice 800. Hurting Kin costs 25 and turns the camp's Hunters on you for a minute; breaking a hearth costs 40; breaking a banner costs 5.
5. /tribalpower standing prints all nine.

chapters.title: Tribal Kin
chapters.text:
Every camp keeps four Kin.

How:
1. Elder: trades from the tribe's table once you are a Guest. Two offers per rank. Stock restocks once per Minecraft day. At Voice, presses a Tribe Mark into your hand.
2. Drummer: every 6 seconds feeds 2 Pulse into a Drumheart, Ley Collector or Pulse Resonator within 8 blocks. Wind Harps, Wave Drums and Ember Horns take none of that beat.
3. Hunter: strikes hostiles within 12 blocks. Hits you for a minute if you hurt Kin.
4. Weaver: walks to a loom or Song Bench and works it for six seconds. That pose is the work; it does not craft for you.
5. Kin wander within 16 blocks of their camp and never despawn. Never hit them.

chapters.title: Kinship Totem
chapters.text:
An extra voice for the Resonator, tracked per tribe rather than per element.

How:
1. Reach Voice with a tribe. The Elder presses a Tribe Mark into your hand.
2. Craft the Mark with that tribe's Resonance Totem and two Spiritweave.
3. Place the Kinship Totem within 8 of a station or Resonator.
4. On a Pulse Resonator it is an extra tribe voice: Quiet kinship still counts; Quiet Resonance Totems do not. On stations and the Loom Anchor it only lends the tribe's element; it is not a seventh voice.
5. A heap still caps at five total. A Voice Ring lets six elements plus all nine tribes add up to fifteen. A Grit-singer Kinship Totem or a Tribe Hearth inside Deep Listening is required for deep, hot and rare, not only rare.

chapters.title: Pad-keepers
chapters.text:
Strand of Soil, voice of Earth. Craft: hearths and caches. Camps stand in plains; a March camp keeps the old road. Favoured offerings: dirt, moss, bread and Echo Shards.

"We never called it dirt. We called it what was left, and we kept it warm."

chapters.title: Grit-singers
chapters.text:
Strand of Stone, voice of Earth. Craft: echo shatter and meshes. Camps stand in mountains; a March camp keeps the old road. Favoured offerings: raw ores, grits and Attuned Echo.

"The mesh does not find the ore. The mesh gives the ore somewhere to land."

chapters.title: Rootbinders
chapters.text:
Strand of Sprout, voice of Water. Craft: living anchors and March flora. Camps stand in forests; a March camp keeps the old road. Favoured offerings: saplings, seeds and Mossback Scale.

"Roots are the only rope the void respects."

chapters.title: Edge-walkers
chapters.text:
Strand of Claw, voice of Fire. Craft: Spiritgear and footholds. Camps stand in taiga; a March camp keeps the old road. Favoured offerings: leather, iron and Rift Tooth.

"Boots first. Then the bridge. Then the courage; it arrives on its own."

chapters.title: Drumhearts
chapters.text:
Strand of Spark, voice of Fire. Craft: drums and Pulse. Camps stand in savanna; a March camp keeps the old road. Favoured offerings: copper, charged Pulse Cells and Bone Chimes.

"The drum is not loud. The drum is steady. Be the drum."

chapters.title: Pattern-weavers
chapters.text:
Strand of Clock, voice of Air. Craft: timed songs and automation. Camps stand in birch woods; a March camp keeps the old road. Favoured offerings: redstone, clocks and Storm Wing.

"A factory is a song that has stopped needing the singer."

chapters.title: Colony-keepers
chapters.text:
Strand of Swarm, voice of Air. Craft: hives and March flowers. Camps stand in flower meadows; a March camp keeps the old road. Favoured offerings: honey, flowers and Lantern Down.

"You do not own a hive. You are on good terms with it."

chapters.title: Seal-carvers
chapters.text:
Strand of Sigil, voice of Spirit. Craft: seals and rites. Camps stand in dark forests; a March camp keeps the old road. Favoured offerings: blank or element seals and Spirit Shards.

"Spirit goes where it is asked politely and stays where it is fed."

chapters.title: Loom-stitchers
chapters.text:
Strand of Spindle, voice of Loom. Craft: gate-paths and the reweave. Camps stand in the March crystal fields only; a March camp keeps the old road. Favoured offerings: March Crystal, Loom Thread and compasses.

"The Loom was never one thread. It was nine agreeing."

chapters.title: Ancestor Hall
chapters.text:
Sunken stone halls in the March steppe and highlands.

How:
1. Find a hall: three rooms under Loom-wood beams with a ladder shaft to the surface.
2. Read every Lore Tablet on the walls. The Codex records them.
3. Two chests hold Loom Thread, echoes, Spiritweave and seals.
4. Hollow Sentinels keep the side rooms — light and a staff help.
5. Next: a Drum Circle in the highlands, and the Crystal Spire for Loom-stitcher trades.

chapters.title: Drum Circle
chapters.text:
Twelve lantern-topped pillars ring a Silent Drum in the March highlands.

How:
1. Bind a return compass. Bring food, Pulse and a Bone Chime.
2. Strike the drum empty-handed or with a Bone Chime: four beats about a second apart (16 to 28 ticks).
3. A wrong beat thuds and resets. Each drum answers once per twenty minutes of real time, and never while its keeper is already awake.
4. A music disc of the circle's four-beat sits in a chest among the pillars; The Unsung carries another.
5. See Walkthrough: wake The Unsung for the fight itself.

chapters.title: The Unsung
chapters.text:
A hollow drum-spirit with two rune arms and a cracked mask. It only wants the rhythm back.

How:
1. Beat (above two thirds): a shockwave every 3 seconds hits everyone within 8 blocks for 6 and knocks back. Sneak to brace for half damage and no knockback. Its swipe deals 10.
2. Chorus: every 8 seconds it calls two Echo Weavers, up to six, and shockwaves every 2.5 seconds. Clear the weavers.
3. Silence (below one third): invulnerable over the drum, slow weaving bolts. Play the four-beat on the Silent Drum to resync: stunned 8 seconds at double damage. Silence returns 12 seconds after each resync.
4. Drops an Unsung Heart, 16 to 24 Loom Thread, 4 Resonant Cores, and a Drum Circle music disc.
5. Leave for 30 seconds and it resets.

chapters.title: Crystal Spire
chapters.text:
A tapering spire of March Crystal in the crystal fields.

How:
1. Find the waystation at its foot: a hearth, a banner, a Loom totem and one Elder of the Spindle tribe.
2. Offer March Crystal, Loom Thread or compasses.
3. Friend standing opens Loom Thread trades.
4. This is the only camp the Loom-stitchers keep.
5. Bind a compass before you wander the crystal fields — Shardbacks shove hard.

chapters.title: Tablet: Pad-keepers' Hearth
chapters.text: We never called it dirt. We called it what was left, and we kept it warm. When the ground fell away we carried it in baskets, a pad at a time, and set a hearth on every pad we saved. Feed the hearth bread and moss. It remembers who fed it.

chapters.title: Tablet: Grit-singers' Mesh
chapters.text: The mesh does not find the ore. The mesh gives the ore somewhere to land. Sing low over raw stone and it loosens; sing lower and it shatters into echo. Our meshes still hang in the halls, humming to nothing. Bring them ore and they will hum to you.

chapters.title: Tablet: Rootbinders' Rope
chapters.text: Roots are the only rope the void respects. We planted the first anchors on the falling islands and bound them island to island, root to root. Half of them held. Plant a sapling in the March soil and you will feel it pull toward the others.

chapters.title: Tablet: Edge-walkers' Boots
chapters.text: Boots first. Then the bridge. Then the courage; it arrives on its own. We walked the rift edge where the thread frayed thinnest and set footholds for the rest. A foothold is iron, leather and a promise not to look down.

chapters.title: Tablet: Drumhearts' Beat
chapters.text: The drum is not loud. The drum is steady. Be the drum. One beat a breath apart, and the copper answers; miss a beat and it forgets you. Every engine in the March still keeps our time. Strike, wait, strike. That is the whole of it.

chapters.title: Tablet: Pattern-weavers' Song
chapters.text: A factory is a song that has stopped needing the singer. We wrote the timings on clock-wheels and moth dust and let the Loom carry the tune. When the Cut came the songs kept playing. Some are playing still. Listen for the click before the hum.

chapters.title: Tablet: Colony-keepers' Hive
chapters.text: You do not own a hive. You are on good terms with it. Offer honey, plant the March flowers, and the swarm will route Pulse through the comb for you. Take without asking and the comb goes quiet. It is very patient about this.

chapters.title: Tablet: Seal-carvers' Rite
chapters.text: Spirit goes where it is asked politely and stays where it is fed. A seal is a polite request carved in stone. A brazier is the meal. We cut blank seals by the thousand before the Cut, and asked for far too much. Ask for a little. Feed it well.

chapters.title: Tablet: Loom-stitchers' Thread
chapters.text: The Loom was never one thread. It was nine agreeing. We held the Spindle and stitched the tribes' strands into one cloth over the sky. When eight pulls became eight arguments, the cloth tore along our seam. We are still stitching. Bring crystal. Bring thread.

chapters.title: Tablet: The Cut
chapters.text: No one struck the Loom. It was pulled from nine sides until one strand gave, and then the rest went like a rope through a hand. The continents fell in the space of a drum-roll. What did not fall drifted into the March and sank slow. Nine tribes, one hall, no one to blame.

chapters.title: Tablet: The Unsung
chapters.text: A drum was carried out of every falling camp so the beat would not stop. The last drum was carried into the circle and no one was left to strike it. Its keeper went hollow waiting. Wake it with the four-beat and it will rise to be struck. Sneak when it beats. Resync it when it goes silent. It only wants the rhythm back.

chapters.title: Tablet: The March
chapters.text: The March is where the thread frayed thinnest and the fallen ground came to rest. Halls lie sunk to the lintel; camps keep time with no one at the drum; crystal grows where the Loom's tension still pools. Walk it with a full Pulse cell and a steady hand. Everything here still answers a beat.

chapters.title: Walkthrough: your first camp
chapters.text:
Goal: Become a Guest of one tribe and open its first trades.

You need
A safe route to a tribe camp and offerings listed on that tribe's page.

Steps
1. Find a tribe camp: a hearth, a banner and four Kin in plains, mountains, forest, taiga, savanna, birch woods, flower meadows or dark forest. The banner colour names the tribe; the tribe pages list what each favours.
2. Read the hearth. Sneak-use the Spirit Codex on it, or simply watch what the Kin carry: bread and moss for Pad-keepers, ores for Grit-singers, saplings for Rootbinders.
3. Offer. Use a favoured item on the Tribe Hearth for +3 standing, or the tribe's reagent for +8. Any food gives +1 and a charged Pulse Cell gives +2 per 10 Pulse (at most 40 Pulse, +8). Seventeen favoured offerings, or seven reagents, reach Guest at 50 and stay under the 60 standing a hearth grants each day.
4. Trade. Use the Elder once you are a Guest. Every trade gives +2, and each rank unlocks two more offers.
5. Keep the peace. Never hit Kin (-25 standing and an angry Hunter for a minute), never break the hearth (-40) and never break the banner (-5). Kills of hostiles within 24 blocks of the hearth earn +1, twenty times a day.
Check: Guest standing with one tribe, its first trades, and a hearth that remembers you. /tribalpower standing prints all nine.
Next: Friend at 150 opens the seal and tablet trades; Voice at 800 earns a Tribe Mark, the key to a Kinship Totem. Offerings alone will not reach Voice in a day.

chapters.title: Walkthrough: the sixth voice
chapters.text:
Goal: Add Loom as your sixth elemental requirement.

You need
Access to the March, a safe return route, food and the materials listed in each linked recipe.

Steps
1. Loot an Ancestor Hall. The sunken halls in the March steppe and highlands keep Loom Thread in their two chests; read the four tablets on the way out.
2. Carve a Loom Seal: a Blank Seal, one Loom Thread and a Spirit Shard, shapeless. Seat it in a Ritual Brazier with Pulse nearby to thread 2 Pulse into your carried cells every two seconds.
3. Build Echo Unweave: March Stone around a Copper Resonator, a Spirit Shard and two Loom Thread. It needs the Loom voice within 8 blocks, which for now only a Kinship Totem of the Loom-stitchers or a Loom-stitcher camp can lend.
4. Wake The Unsung at a Drum Circle (see that walkthrough) and take its Unsung Heart.
5. Craft the Loom totem: four March Crystal, two Loom Thread, two March Planks around the Unsung Heart. Place it within 8 blocks of the Unweave and of a Pulse Resonator.
Check: the sixth voice. Unweave turns ingots back to echoes, cores to ingots, Spiritweave to wool and damaged Spiritgear into one Manifested Ingot; the Resonator counts one more distinct voice.
Next: the Sixfold Staff's Loom voice (Tether and Stitch) and the Ley Binding rite, which needs the Loom seal.

chapters.title: Walkthrough: wake The Unsung
chapters.text:
Goal: Complete the Drum Circle encounter and collect its crafting materials.

You need
Food, armor, charged Pulse cells, a Bone Chime and a tested return route.

Steps
1. Prepare: full Pulse cells, food, a Bone Chime, and a bound return route. Bring a friend if you can; the fight lasts a few minutes.
2. Find a Drum Circle in the March highlands: twelve lantern pillars around a Silent Drum.
3. Beat four times. Strike the drum empty-handed or with the chime, about one second apart (16 to 28 ticks). A wrong beat thuds and resets the count. The drum answers once per twenty minutes and never while its keeper is awake.
4. Beat phase: every three seconds a shockwave hits everyone within 8 blocks for 6 and knocks back. Sneak just before it lands to brace: half damage, no knockback. Its swipe deals 10, so keep the drum between you.
5. Chorus, below two thirds health: it calls two Echo Weavers every eight seconds, up to six, and shockwaves every 2.5 seconds. Clear the weavers before they slow you.
6. Silence, below one third: it hovers invulnerable over the drum and casts slow weaving bolts. Walk to the drum and play the four-beat again to resync it: eight seconds stunned at double damage. Silence returns twelve seconds after each resync, so repeat.
Check: an Unsung Heart, 16 to 24 Loom Thread, 4 Resonant Cores, and a Drum Circle music disc. Leaving for thirty seconds resets the fight.
Next: the Loom totem (The sixth voice) and the Loom-stitcher trades at the Crystal Spire.

chapters.title: Walkthrough: your first rite
chapters.text:
Goal: Use a tablet and a powered brazier to change the weather.

You need
A Ritual Brazier, four Rite Pedestals, Ritual Chalk, the correct elemental seal, a rite tablet and enough stored Pulse for its full cost.

Steps
1. Choose the rite. Rain Calling needs the Water seal and 400 Pulse; Sky Clearing the Air seal and 400. Dawn Calling (Fire, 800) and the land rites cost more. Start with rain.
2. Carve the tablet: two stone, the rite's creature reagent (a Reed Fang for rain) and the matching seal, shapeless. The seal is handed back.
3. Seat the seal. Use the Water Seal on a Ritual Brazier; the brazier's usual blessing still runs, and the seal stays reusable.
4. Draw the circle. Four Rite Pedestals on the diagonals, chalk joining them. A tablet rite without that circle names the missing pieces and spends nothing.
5. Gather 400 Pulse within 8 blocks of the brazier: a Drumheart holding enough stored Pulse, a Resonator with a good catalyst, or several generators together. A Pulse Gauge or the Codex diagnostics show the total. A cell in your pocket is not in range.
6. Cast. Sneak-use the tablet on the brazier. If the lattice holds less than the cost nothing is spent; otherwise the tablet is consumed and the Pulse drawn.
Check: twenty minutes of rain (or forty minutes of clear sky), stronger Ley Collectors, and a brazier that knows how to answer tablets.
Next: Green Blessing over your farm (Earth, 600), Still Night around the camp (Spirit, 600), or Ley Binding between two distant totems (Loom, 1,200).

chapters.title: Walkthrough: bond a familiar
chapters.text:
Goal: Bond an adult animal and use its ability.

You need
A Bonding Charm for the chosen species and access to an adult animal.

Steps
1. Craft a Bonding Charm: two Spiritweave, a Spirit Shard and one reagent of the animal you want (Lantern Down, Mossback Scale or Dawn Velvet). Brush an adult of that species to get the reagent.
2. Find an adult Lantern Fox (forests, dusk), Mossback (swamps) or Dawn Stag (forests, dawn). Young animals cannot be bonded. Sneak-use a Ley Lens on it: two of the same species will not share the same threads.
3. Use the charm on it. Three tries in five succeed with hearts; a failed charm is kept, so try again. Success does not reroll the lattice.
4. Follow and stay. The familiar follows within ten blocks and teleports to you past twelve. Quiet Thread follows from eight and stops at two. Sneak-use it to wait or follow. A Mossback with an empty hand opens its saddlebag; sneak-use while holding an item to wait or follow. It never despawns and ignores your blows.
5. Learn its trick. Fox: an invisible Spirit Light travels with it, Night Vision within eight blocks, and ore glints only you can see. Mossback: sneak-use with an empty hand for a nine-slot saddlebag (twelve with Deep Pocket). Stag: use it to ride without a saddle, steer with your gaze, hold jump to leap, sneak to dismount.
6. Brush it. A bonded animal sheds double reagent, once a minute. Breed two of the same species when you want stronger threads.
7. Remnants are a later trick. Reach Voice with their tribe, then read Hostile bonds and Combat and company. One fighter and two helpers may follow.
Check: a companion that lights, carries or carries you, and a renewable reagent supply.
Next: Rootbinders favour Mossback Scale and Colony-keepers Lantern Down, so a brushed familiar also buys standing.

chapters.title: Walkthrough: seat a Resonator
chapters.text:
Goal: make your first automatic Pulse supply.

You need
Echo Shatter, a charged Drumheart, stone, an Earth Resonance Totem, a Fire Resonance Totem and a Pulse Resonator.

Steps
1. Put the Drumheart and Earth totem beside Echo Shatter. Keep both within 8 blocks.
2. Charge the drum with several steady beats. Put stone in Shatter and wait for an Echo Shard. Cobblestone gives gravel instead.
3. Place the Pulse Resonator on clear floor. Use the shard on it to install the reusable catalyst.
4. Put Earth and Fire totems beside it. Count different elements, not the number of blocks.
5. Wait a second and inspect stored Pulse. It should begin increasing.

Check
The catalyst remains installed and the generator makes power without manual beats. The starter rate is small; a demanding station can use it faster than it is generated.

If it does not work
Check that the shard is installed, both elements are in range and redstone is not pausing the Resonator. Use Codex diagnostics.

Next
Read Walkthrough: run a Conductor when you want to distribute stored power.

chapters.title: Walkthrough: run a Conductor
chapters.text:
Goal: Move stored Pulse into a linked pair of totem buffers.

You need
Two Resonance Totems, Ritual Chalk, a Lattice Conductor and a charged generator.

Steps
1. Place two Resonance Totems within 16 of each other, and a Drumheart (or Ley Collector, or Resonator) nearby.
2. Hold Ritual Chalk. Click totem A, then totem B. You should see "Lattice link sealed". Clicking the same totem twice cancels the pending mark.
3. Place a Lattice Conductor within 8 of those totems and within 8 of the generator.
4. Put Pulse in the generator: strike the Drumheart, or seat a catalyst in the Resonator.
5. Wait one second, or click the Conductor. It should report a lattice network and Pulse routed into totem buffers.
6. If a Song Bench on the lattice wants help, the Conductor fills it first. Ancestral Caches beside the totems will swap Echo items with benches every two seconds while Pulse is present.
7. A lever on the Conductor pauses it. Sneak-use the Spirit Codex on it to hear network size, last Pulse pushed, and what is missing.
Check: Pulse walking from your generators into totems and workshops instead of sitting in one drum.
Next: Ley Binding to join distant totems, and wireless relays when you need items rather than Pulse.

chapters.title: Walkthrough: totem-bound gear
chapters.text:
Goal: Link a piece of equipment to an element, then upgrade it in order.

You need
Spiritgear or Spiritweave armor, a matching Resonance Totem and a Pulse Cell with at least 40 Pulse.

Steps
1. Craft Spiritgear (Manifested Ingots) or Spiritweave armor. Fresh pieces are diamond-hard, rank 0, unlinked.
2. Carry a charged Pulse Cell (40 Pulse to link).
3. Place a Resonance Totem. Sneak-use the piece on it. The action bar names the voice. Empty-handed clicks still read the totem.
4. Rank it: Echo Attune with a Fire totem (0 to 1), Echo Bind with Water (1 to 2), Echo Manifest with Spirit (2 to 3). Bind refuses rank 0; you cannot skip.
5. Mix voices if you want: a Fire hood is fire resist, not night sight. A full linked set costs 12 Pulse every four seconds.
6. Loom voice needs a Loom totem (see The sixth voice). Unweave of a damaged tool returns one Manifested Ingot and forgets rank and voice.
Check: gear that answers a totem, and a rank path through the Echo stations.
Next: Recipes in this book list every rank formula. JEI, when installed, lists them too. Totem-bound gear in this Codex names the tool perks.

chapters.title: Walkthrough: found a camp
chapters.text:
Goal: Create a shared group for storage and device access.

You need
A camp name and, for inviting players by item, a Camp Charter.

Steps
1. Found it: /tribalpower camp create <name>. You become its first member.
2. Invite. Craft a Camp Charter (paper, Spiritweave, Spirit Shard) and use it on a player, or run /tribalpower camp invite <player>. Invitations last five minutes; the invitee accepts with /tribalpower camp join <name>.
3. Share the vault. Open any Deep Cache or Wayfarer Satchel: sneak-use switches between your personal vault and the shared 54-slot camp vault.
4. Share the devices. Members count as owners of each other's camp devices: cradles, tenders, anchors and locked menus open for all of you.
5. Budget anchors. The camp shares twelve Wayanchors per dimension instead of thirty-two each, so agree on which chunks matter.
6. Manage it: /tribalpower camp info, rename, kick and leave. A quarter of every member's tribe standing lands on the camp, and an Elder trades at the camp's rank when it beats your own.
