Check: a named camp with one vault, shared devices and pooled tribe standing.
Next: the Shared camps teaching for the fine print, and Kinship Totems to lend your camp every tribe's voice.

chapters.title: Placement is the ritual
chapters.text:
Pattern machines only work when their blocks sit in the right shape. Crouch and right-click the Codex on the anchor: it names missing pieces and shows ghosts.

How:
1. Pick an anchor: Stone Font, Resonance Mesh, Ritual Brazier, Pulse Resonator, Echo station, or Gate Keystone.
2. Build the pattern around it. Any rotation works.
3. Sneak-use the Spirit Codex on the anchor.
4. It names the tier, the facing, and the first three things that are missing, with ghosts where they should go.
5. Brace corners with Anchor Stones when a tier asks for them.

chapters.title: Ritual Mark
chapters.text:
Marks are what join a pattern together.

How:
1. Craft Ritual Chalk — four sticks, ten uses each.
2. Click the top of a solid block to draw a mark. Each draw spends one use.
3. Click the mark again to rub it out. Erasing costs nothing.
4. Click two Resonance Totems (within 16) to seal a Lattice link; a successful link spends one use.
5. Marks drop nothing when broken, because the chalk already paid.

Creative mode does not spend uses.

chapters.title: Anchor Stone
chapters.text:
They brace the corners of a pattern and do nothing else: no Pulse, no inventory, no upkeep.

How:
1. Craft four March Stone and an Echo Shard into four Anchor Stones.
2. Place them on the corners the Codex ghosts show.
3. A pattern that has them is a tier higher than one that does not.
4. They are not generators. Leave them alone after they sit.
5. Break one and the pattern drops a tier until you replace it.

chapters.title: Stone Font
chapters.text:
The Stone Font makes cobblestone, stone or obsidian from Pulse. Unbraced cobble is cheap enough for a hand-drummed Drumheart. Font cobble is for hammers and building — Echo Shards still need smelted stone in Echo Shatter.

How:
1. Craft four stone, two Echo Shards and a Drumheart into a font.
2. Place it with four chalk marks around it: cobble every two seconds at 4 Pulse a second. Pack settings do not touch cobble.
3. Brace the corners with Anchor Stones and bring the Earth voice: stone at 16 Pulse a second before pack settings.
4. Both obsidian paths need braced Earth. Add Fire and Water both: obsidian at 24 Pulse a second before pack settings. Or feed 250 mB of water and 250 mB of lava for the same obsidian at 6 before pack settings. Unbraced piping does nothing.
5. Below y 0 it gives the deepslate of each tier instead. Rank the font like any other workshop: faster asks, more Pulse a second. The default 2.0 consumption multiplier doubles stone and obsidian, not cobble. A pack pit-speed setting shortens every ask without raising Pulse a second, so it also cheapens each block.

chapters.title: Listening Pit
chapters.text:
The Resonance Mesh turns substrate plus a sample into ore. Earth is required. The sample is a filter, not an ingredient.

How:
1. Lay stone or deepslate in the pit footprint.
2. Brace four corners with Anchor Stones. Chalk from each edge to the middle.
3. Set a Resonance Mesh at the centre, an Ancestral Cache beside it, and the Earth voice within eight blocks.
4. Hopper substrate in from the sides. Seat a sample on top. Take ore from the bottom — or let the mesh empty itself into the cache.
5. Friend standing with the Grit-singers is required even for common ore. A stranger's pit stalls. The mesh holds a 200 Pulse buffer so a bursty generator does not stutter the cycle. Rank the mesh like any other workshop.

chapters.title: Deep Listening
chapters.text:
The seven by seven doubles the corner bracing and opens the deep, hot and rare bands.

How:
1. Expand the pit to seven by seven. Double the corner bracing.
2. Seat a totem at each cardinal edge.
3. Stand a Tribe Hearth or a Grit-singer Kinship Totem inside the pattern. Deep, hot and rare all need it; common does not.
4. Grit-singer standing: Friend for common (even on a small pit). Kin for deep and hot. Voice for rare.
5. Hot wants Fire. Rare wants Spirit. The Codex names what you still lack.

chapters.title: What the ground offers
chapters.text:
The pit calls up exactly what a silk-touch mining trip would: the raw item for a metal, the ore block for a gem.

How:
1. Common: coal, copper and iron at 10 seconds and 28 Pulse a second on two stone, before pack settings.
2. Deep: gold, redstone and lapis at 15 seconds and 32, on two March Stone. Quartz is not in this band.
3. Hot: the Nether's quartz and gold at 20 seconds and 36, with Fire.
4. Rare: diamond, emerald and any metal or gem the grit scan found, at 40 seconds and 24, on four March Stone and a Spirit Shard.
5. Those Pulse figures are before pack settings. The default 2.0 consumption multiplier doubles them, so one iron cycle is 560 Pulse at the shipped default. A pack pit-speed setting shortens the cycle without raising Pulse a second, so it also cheapens each cycle. Mining stays cheaper per ingot.

chapters.title: Sample and substrate
chapters.text:
A sample is a filter, never an ingredient.

How:
1. Seat a sample on top of the mesh. It is not consumed.
2. A material it names weighs six times as much as anything else in the band.
3. A sample the band does not hold is ignored, and the Codex says so.
4. Substrates are renewable on purpose — stone from a Stone Font, March Stone from cobble.
5. One iron cycle spends 280 Pulse on two stone before pack settings (560 at the default 2.0 multiplier) and returns raw iron. Mining still costs less Pulse per ingot.

chapters.title: Voices at the pit
chapters.text:
Each voice trades one thing for another; none of them is a plain multiplier.

How:
1. Earth is required.
2. Water washes for 250 mB a cycle and gives one extra output every third cycle.
3. Air quickens the cycle to about 0.65 time and charges about 1.55 times as much Pulse a second — Pulse per item does not move.
4. Fire opens the hot band (Nether quartz and gold) at 36 Pulse a second before pack settings. Spirit listens a band deeper and opens the rare one.
5. The Loom halves the substrate, rounded up.

chapters.title: Way Gate
chapters.text:
A five by five ring without its corners, keystone at the bottom centre.

How:
1. Six March Stone, two copper and an Echo Shard make four Gate Frames.
2. Four frames, a Resonant Core, a Spirit Shard and a Pulse Cell make the keystone.
3. Build the ring. Charge the keystone from a Pulse Cell (up to 100 Pulse each use).
4. Light it by hand or with a struck signal: 400 Pulse out of its own 600.
5. Twenty Pulse carries anything that walks in — players, mobs and dropped items. A one-second cooldown stops bounce-back.

chapters.title: Far Gate
chapters.text:
A taller frame around a three by four interior. Crossing dimensions sits behind The Unsung. Lighting costs more than a Way Gate.

How:
1. Build the taller ring. Brace four Anchor Stones at the corners of its footprint.
2. Place the Loom voice within eight blocks.
3. Craft a Gate Sigil: Blank Seal, Loom Thread and a Spirit Shard.
4. Sneak-use the sigil on one keystone to write that gate down, then use it on the other to tie the pair both ways.
5. Light it: 1,200 Pulse out of its own 2,000. Travel is 120 Pulse with a two-second cooldown afterwards.

chapters.title: Keeping the way
chapters.text:
A gate always lands you inside the far gate's own interior and never terraforms.

How:
1. Link Way Gates locally: sneak-use an unbound Waystone Compass on the first keystone, then sneak-use that bound compass on the second. Chalk from one keystone to the other within 64 also works.
2. If there is nowhere to stand the trip refuses and the Pulse comes back.
3. The far end is held loaded for ten seconds around your arrival, so an unloaded partner still answers.
4. Break a keystone and its partner is released; anyone standing near it is told.
5. /tribalpower gate list and /tribalpower gate unlink read and cut the threads.

chapters.title: Ember Horn
chapters.text:
The Drumhearts' craft. Feed it furnace fuel.

How:
1. Place the horn. Hopper, relay or hand-feed any furnace fuel.
2. Burn time divided by twenty is Pulse, delivered at up to 20 a second.
3. Coal is 80, a coal block 800, a lava bucket 1,000, a blaze rod 120.
4. Unranked, the cap is 20 a second. More fuel does not raise it. Rank adds 15% Pulse a second per rank. The horn holds 1,000 Pulse.
5. Horns are a tribe craft. Nothing you can automate turns fuel into more fuel than it burns.

chapters.title: Wind Harp
chapters.text:
The Pattern-weavers' craft, and free, so it is capped instead.

How:
1. Place the harp under open sky. Under a roof it makes nothing at all.
2. One Pulse a second as a base and one more under open sky.
3. One more above y 128 and two above y 192. One more in rain or two in a storm.
4. Six a second is the unranked cap. Rank adds 15% Pulse a second per rank. The harp holds 1,000 Pulse.
5. Harps within twelve blocks divide it between them, so a wall of harps is a wall of decorations.

chapters.title: Wave Drum
chapters.text:
The Rootbinders' craft. It makes Pulse from water; it is not a spare tank.

How:
1. Place it beside water for 3 Pulse a second, shared with any drum within eight blocks.
2. Give it its own water instead — a bucket, a Spirit Cistern, or a fluid relay — and it makes 10 a second for 100 mB a second. Its internal tank holds 4,000 mB of water only. The drum holds 1,000 Pulse.
3. Rain doubles either tier. Rank adds 15% Pulse a second per rank.
4. Break it: the dropped drum keeps that internal water. Pair a Tide Pump if you need the water to move after it arrives. Relays and the Tide Pump move fluid; they are not storage.
5. Spring Calling on a nearby Spirit Cistern is how the water refills itself.

chapters.title: Wake Bell
chapters.text:
The Seal-carvers' craft. A mob farm that pays Pulse.

How:
1. Place the bell within sixteen blocks of the deaths.
2. Twenty Pulse for a hostile death, five for a passive one.
3. A reservoir of 2,000 lets out at most eight a second unranked. Rank adds 15% Pulse a second per rank. A big farm fills it and then idles.
4. Only the nearest bell hears a death, so stacking bells buys nothing.
5. A Pulse Cairn turns those bursts into the steady draw a Listening Pit wants.

chapters.title: Loom Anchor
chapters.text:
The Loom Anchor makes 1 Pulse a second per distinct totem voice within 8, up to 6. Quiet totems still count. A live Ley Binding nearby doubles the rate.

How:
1. Place the Anchor within eight blocks of your totems.
2. One Pulse a second per distinct voice, to a maximum of six. Quiet totems still count.
3. A live Ley Binding nearby doubles it.
4. Kinship Totems lend the tribe's element into that six-voice set; they are not a seventh voice. A Grit-singer kinship beside an Earth totem does nothing extra.
5. Rank it in Echo Attune, Bind, then Manifest for 15% Pulse a second per rank, not the workshop 118%. It holds 1,000 Pulse.

chapters.title: Pulse Cairn
chapters.text:
A Pulse Cairn stores up to 4,000 Pulse and pulls surplus from nearby generators. Stack up to five in a column.

How:
1. Craft six March Stone, two Bound Echoes and a Pulse Cell.
2. Each cairn holds 4,000 Pulse and swallows up to 200 Pulse a second from nearby generators.
3. Stack up to five in a column; the sixth stone is just a stone.
4. A comparator reads how full it is.
5. Sit one beside a Wake Bell and a Listening Pit so bursts become a steady draw.

chapters.title: Spring Calling
chapters.text:
Spring Calling marks a placed Spirit Cistern so it refills water. Every tablet rite needs the Rite Circle, including this one. The Water Seal is returned.

How:
1. Draw the circle: brazier in the middle, four Rite Pedestals on the diagonals, chalk joining them.
2. Carve the tablet: two stone, a Spirit Reed and the Water Seal. The seal comes back.
3. Seat the Water Seal in the brazier. Place a Spirit Cistern beside it.
4. Sneak-use the tablet on the brazier. Spend 300 Pulse. The cistern becomes a spring: 100 mB a second for ten minutes.
5. Repeat when it runs dry. Moving the cistern ends the spring; water already inside stays on the item. March-side lava stays a manual haul.

chapters.title: Draw the circle
chapters.text:
A brazier's standing blessing needs only a seated seal and its matching totem. Every tablet rite needs this circle, including Spring Calling.

How:
1. Brazier in the middle.
2. Four Rite Pedestals on the diagonals, chalk joining them.
3. Seat four totems of the rite's own voice on the cardinals and it costs a quarter less and lasts twice as long.
4. Crouch and right-click the Codex on the brazier if a pedestal is missing: it shows ghosts.
5. If the circle is incomplete the tablet is not spent.

chapters.title: A rite on a clock
chapters.text:
A Rite Pedestal holds and shows one item. A comparator reads whether it is occupied.

How:
1. A relay restocks a pedestal with a tablet.
2. A Heartbeat plate (or a lever) strikes the brazier.
3. The rite fires and spends the tablet.
4. The comparator reports the pedestal empty, and the relay fills it again.
5. The base uses the same actions you can do by hand: no hidden extra inventory.

chapters.title: Metals and gems
chapters.text:
Grit is crushed metal waiting to be smelted. Gems shatter straight out of silk-touched ore.

How:
1. Metal: raw item or silk-touched ore into Echo Shatter to grit (4 seconds and 20 Pulse a second before pack settings), then grit to ingot in a furnace, blast furnace or Ember Kiln.
2. Gem or mineral: silk-touched ore shatters straight into the gem at twice the ore's own drop.
3. Coal, diamond, emerald and quartz give two. Redstone and lapis give eight. The gem itself is never an input.
4. Modded metals ride one Mineral Grit item that names its own material, and light up with no datapack.
5. Sit Shatter on a Kiln, Output into Input, and grit walks down.

chapters.title: Voice Ring
chapters.text:
A heap of totems counts at most five voices. Six-voice resonance only counts when the voices are arranged.

How:
1. Place the Resonator.
2. On the same floor, three blocks away at the cardinals and diagonals, stand Resonance Totems (eight slots on a square grid).
3. Seat a catalyst. Distinct voices among those arranged totems all count, including the sixth. Only Answered Resonance Totems count; Quiet voices do not.
4. Sneak-use the Spirit Codex on the Resonator to see ghosts of any missing ring slots.
5. A heap nearby still works for five voices total if they are Answered, kinship included. The ring is what lets six elements plus kinship add up.

chapters.title: Shatter Array
chapters.text:
Centre an Echo station in a five by five with four totems of the recipe's own attunement at the corners and an Ancestral Cache beneath.

How:
1. Place the station. Four matching totems at the corners of a five by five.
2. Put an Ancestral Cache under it.
3. The station then costs a quarter less Pulse and empties itself into the cache.
4. Entirely optional. Every station works exactly as before without it.
5. Sneak-use the Codex on the station to see the ghosts.

chapters.title: Camp hands
chapters.text:
Pattern-weavers taught the camp to keep working after the singer left. Four hands sit beside the Grove Tender: the Seal Loom, the Tide Pump, the Wind Snare and the Ward Drum.

How:
1. Raise Pulse within 8 — a Drumheart, Ley Collector, Pulse Resonator, or a voice-craft such as a Wind Harp.
2. Place the hand. Each one drinks Pulse only when it actually works.
3. A constant redstone signal pauses it. A comparator reads what it is doing.
4. Rank it in Echo Attune, Bind, then Manifest. Ranked hands beat faster. Pulse per move stays the same, so the lattice feels the extra speed.
5. Open the next pages for each hand, then the walkthroughs.

chapters.title: Seal Loom
chapters.text:
The Seal Loom copies a crafting-table recipe onto a Recipe Seal, then crafts that recipe automatically for 6 Pulse each result. The seal is reusable.

How:
1. Craft a Recipe Seal from a Blank Seal and paper.
2. Place the Seal Loom. Hopper ingredients into the three-by-three from the sides or top.
3. Seat the Recipe Seal in the dedicated seal slot beside the grid, not in the centre of the three-by-three.
4. Arrange the crafting-table recipe in the grid. Sneak-use the loom empty-handed. The seal remembers that recipe.
5. Keep matching ingredients in the grid. Every second it spends 6 Pulse and weaves one result. Rank shortens that second; Pulse per craft stays 6.

chapters.title: Tide Pump
chapters.text:
The Tide Pump moves fluid between two tanks. It does not store fluid. Breaking it does not keep a reserve.

How:
1. Place tanks on both faces — Spirit Cisterns, or any fluid handler. Do not use this pump as storage; breaking it does not keep a reserve.
2. The arrow face is the front. By default it draws from the front and pushes into the back.
3. Sneak-use to reverse: now it pushes into the front.
4. Each second it moves 250 mB for 4 Pulse. Rank shortens that second; Pulse per 250 mB stays 4.
5. Click empty-handed to read the current direction. A lever pauses it. Pair it with a Cistern or a Wave Drum when the water should stay put.

chapters.title: Wind Snare
chapters.text:
The Wind Snare picks up dropped item stacks in range and stores them like a chest.

How:
1. Place it near a farm, a shatter station, or anywhere items fall.
2. Keep 2 Pulse nearby per stack it catches, up to eight stacks a second, within 8 blocks.
3. Rank shortens that second. Pulse per stack stays 2.
4. Open it like a chest, or hopper the catch out of any face.
5. A lever pauses both the catch and the hoppers. It does not steal from other inventories.

chapters.title: Ward Drum
chapters.text:
The Ward Drum spends Pulse to damage and shove one hostile per beat inside 8 blocks. It never targets players.

How:
1. Place it where hostiles walk. It listens in an 8-block sphere.
2. Keep 8 Pulse nearby. Each second it hits one hostile for 4 magic and a shove. Rank shortens that second; Pulse per strike stays 8.
3. Players are never the target.
4. A lever silences it. A comparator reads 15 on a hit, 0 while it waits.
5. It is a watch, not a farm. Pair a Wake Bell if the deaths should pay Pulse back.

chapters.title: Song Thread
chapters.text:
Redstone is a shout. Song Thread is a hummed line through the air.

How:
1. Craft Song Thread from redstone and Loom Thread.
2. Place it. It carries 0 to 15 in all six directions and decays by one per block.
3. Vanilla dust, levers, plates, Song Vines and comparators all speak to it.
4. Snap song plates onto faces along the line.

A wall of thread is a wall of song. Keep the line short if you need a full 15 at the far end. For a tendril that hugs stone, see Song Vine.

chapters.title: Song Vine
chapters.text:
A Pattern-weaver's song follows the stone. Song Vine is a tendril that crawls every face of a block.

How:
1. Craft eight vines from one Song Thread and a Spirit Reed.
2. Click a solid face. The vine sits in the air cell on that face.
3. Click an existing vine with another vine to add a second face on the same cell — floor and wall, or every side of a cube.
4. Power decays by one per step, including around corners onto a neighbouring face.
5. It speaks to Song Thread, song plates, vanilla dust and comparators.

Break the block to pick up one vine per face. Relays still carry items; vines carry only the song.

chapters.title: Verse Call and Answer
chapters.text:
Sixteen verses. Two plates singing the same verse hear each other without a vine.

How:
1. Snap a Verse Call onto a face. It reads redstone from every side except its facing.
2. Snap a Verse Answer onto a face within 32 blocks, same world. It sings out of its facing.
3. Sneak-use either plate to cycle verse 1 to 16. Click empty-handed to read the verse and the strength.
4. The Answer copies that strength; it is not always 15. Several Calls of one verse: the Answer takes the loudest.
5. A mismatched verse stays silent. Relays still move items; these plates move only redstone.

Air Seal in the Call, Bone Chime in the Answer. Pattern-weavers favour clocks and Storm Wing.

chapters.title: Song plates
chapters.text:
Thirteen plates. Each does one job. The facing is the output.

How:
1. Snap a plate onto a solid face, the same way you snap a relay.
2. Binary plates (Chorus, Gathering, Discord, Hush) read left and right of the facing.
3. Unary plates (Inverse, Echo, Drift, Strike, Chance, Tally, Verse) read the back.
4. Memory reads left to set and right to clear.
5. Heartbeat needs no input. Sneak-use Heartbeat, Drift or Tally to change the count.

The next pages name each plate. Pattern-weavers favour redstone, clocks and Storm Wing.

chapters.title: Chorus, Gathering, Discord, Hush
chapters.text:
Four ways two voices can agree.

How:
1. Chorus (AND) sings only when left and right are both live.
2. Gathering (OR) sings when either side is live.
3. Discord (XOR) sings when the sides disagree.
4. Hush (NAND) sings unless both sides are live.

Output is 15 or 0 from the facing. Place Song Thread on that face to carry the answer.

chapters.title: Inverse and Echo
chapters.text:
One voice, turned or carried.

How:
1. Inverse (NOT) sings while the back is quiet, and hushes when the back is live.
2. Echo (BUFFER) copies the back: live stays live.

Use Inverse to turn a Pulse Threshold into a 'too empty' alarm. Use Echo to strengthen a fading Song Thread.

chapters.title: Memory, Tally, Verse
chapters.text:
These plates store a redstone state. Memory holds on or off. Tally counts pulses. Verse steps through four strengths.

How:
1. Memory: a live left sets it; a live right clears it. Output stays until told otherwise.
2. Tally: each rising edge on the back adds one. Output 15 once the count meets the threshold. Sneak-use to cycle the threshold 1 to 8. A rising left resets the count.
3. Verse: it starts emitting 4 with no pulse. Each rising edge on the back steps to 8, then 12, then 15, then back to 4. A comparator reads the same number.
4. A rite-on-a-clock loop is Memory plus Heartbeat plus a Rite Pedestal comparator.
5. Verse Call and Answer are a different pair: the Answer copies the Call's strength. See that walkthrough.

chapters.title: Heartbeat, Drift, Strike, Chance
chapters.text:
Heartbeat is a repeating pulse. Drift waits before copying. Strike fires once on a rising edge. Chance is a coin flip.

How:
1. Heartbeat pulses 15 for one tick, then rests. Sneak-use cycles 20, 40, 80, 160 ticks, then back to 20.
2. Drift copies the back, but only after it has stayed live for 4, 8, 16 or 32 ticks (sneak-use to cycle).
3. Strike emits one tick of 15 on a rising back, then goes quiet. That is the Drumheart's struck-signal language.
4. Chance flips a coin on each rising back: 15 or 0 until the back falls.
5. A one-second Heartbeat on a Drumheart is a 24-Pulse beat if the edge lands in tempo.

chapters.title: Walkthrough: tend a grove
chapters.text:
Goal: Automatically plant and harvest a small crop plot.

You need
A Grove Tender, seeds, suitable soil, water for crops that need it, and nearby Pulse generation.

Steps
1. Craft the Grove Tender (Earth Seal, hoe, copper, Bound Echo, planks).
2. Till a 9-by-9 of farmland (or dirt for saplings, sand for cactus). Place the tender yourself in the middle at crop height so it is claimed.
3. Put Pulse within 8 — a Drumheart, Ley Collector, Pulse Resonator, or a voice-craft such as a Wind Harp. Hopper wheat seeds into the top.
4. Wait. It plants for 4 Pulse, then harvests and replants ripe wheat for 12, keeping one seed.
5. For trees: hopper saplings. It plants, urges growth for 16 Pulse, then takes logs and leaves above.
6. For cane: hopper sugar cane onto sand or dirt beside water. It cuts the top of a three-high stalk.
Check: a bed that plants, grows and harvests without you standing there.
Next: a Wind Snare beside it to catch anything that still drops, and a Seal Loom for the harvest.

chapters.title: Walkthrough: imprint a seal
chapters.text:
Goal: automatically craft sticks from planks.

You need
A Seal Loom, a Recipe Seal, two planks of a type that can craft sticks, and a generator within 8 blocks holding at least 6 Pulse per craft.

Steps
1. Open the Seal Loom. Put the Recipe Seal in its dedicated seal slot, outside the nine-slot crafting grid.
2. Place one plank above another in the grid, just like the crafting-table recipe for sticks. Do not use sticks as the input.
3. Close the screen. Crouch and right-click the loom with an empty hand to record the matching recipe on the seal.
4. Inspect the seal tooltip: it should name the stick recipe.
5. Supply Pulse and leave output space. The loom consumes the two planks and places four sticks in its output. The Recipe Seal remains.
6. Refill the same two grid slots to repeat. A hopper can insert items, but you still need the recipe's correct arrangement. Test a single batch before connecting bulk storage.

Check
You get four sticks, spend 6 Pulse, and keep the seal. A redstone signal pauses crafting.

If it does not work
Check the dedicated seal slot, the two vertically aligned planks, stored power and free output space. Changing ingredients does not automatically change the recorded recipe.

chapters.title: Walkthrough: a song clock
chapters.text:
Goal: give a Drumheart a steady automatic beat.

You need
A Drumheart, a Heartbeat plate, solid blocks to support the plate, and Song Thread. A Pulse Gauge is optional.

Steps
1. Place the drum on your platform. Place the Heartbeat plate on a supported face nearby.
2. Crouch and use the plate until its interval reads 20 ticks, or one second.
3. Connect the plate's output side to the drum with Song Thread.
4. Watch the drum for several beats. Its stored Pulse should increase when no machine is spending it.
5. Add a Pulse Gauge if you want to turn the stored amount into a redstone signal.

Check
A steady one-second rising edge earns 24 Pulse. Rapid pulses give less power or are ignored.

If it does not work
Check the plate's orientation, support block and output connection. Remove unintended constant power. Test the clock and drum before adding thresholds or memory plates.

Next
Read the logic pages to pause machines when their inputs or power reserves run low.

chapters.title: Walkthrough: keep a cistern
chapters.text:
Goal: store one fluid so it survives a move and can feed a Wave Drum or Tide Pump.

You need
A Spirit Cistern and a bucket of the fluid you want to keep. A lever, a comparator, and a Tide Pump or fluid relay are optional.

Steps
1. Craft the cistern from copper and glass and place it.
2. Right-click with a bucket. Empty-handed click should read 1,000 of 16,000 mB. It holds one fluid only, 16 buckets in all.
3. Standard pipes, a Tide Pump or a fluid relay can fill and drain it. Relays and the Tide Pump move fluid; they are not tanks.
4. Power it with a lever to lock filling and draining, including remote relays. Stored fluid stays.
5. Put a comparator against it, facing away: 0 empty, then 1 to 15 as it fills.
6. Break it. The dropped cistern keeps the fluid. Place it again and the tank is still full. A Wave Drum also keeps its internal water tank. Relays and the Tide Pump are not tanks.
7. Optional: Spring Calling at a nearby brazier marks this placed cistern a spring. Moving it ends the spring; water already inside still rides on the item.

Check
The comparator reads fullness, a lever stops pipes, and picking the cistern up does not empty it.

If it does not work
Empty-handed click should name the fluid and mB. A redstone lock refuses buckets and pipes. A second fluid will not mix until the tank is empty. Sneak-use this book on the cistern.

Next
Read Wave Drum if the water should make Pulse, Tide Pump if it should move, and Spring Calling when you want it to refill without buckets.

chapters.title: Walkthrough: raise a Ley Collector
chapters.text:
Goal: make Pulse from landscape instead of standing at a drum.

You need
A Ley Collector, open sky, and optionally a Ley Lens.

Steps
1. Place the collector under open sky for the sky bonus. A roof loses sky, rain and storm; water, plants, voices, a hearth and animals still add.
2. Keep it within 8 blocks of the machines you want to feed.
3. Each beat starts at 1. Open sky adds 1 by day or 3 at night; rain 2; thunder 1 more; water up to 4; plants up to 4; totem voices up to 3; a hearth 1; animals up to 2; The March 2; a full moon 1. Cap 16.
4. It adds Pulse every two seconds. The Ley Lens total is that beat, not Pulse a second.
5. A redstone signal pauses generation. Rank it in Echo Attune, Bind, then Manifest for 15% Pulse a second per rank, not the workshop 118%. Sneak-use a Ley Lens on it to print the exact factor breakdown.

Check
Stored Pulse rises every two seconds from the landscape. You do not have to stand there. A roofed collector is weaker, not dead.

If it does not work
Remove the roof. Check redstone. Sneak-use this book on the collector.

Next
Read Keeping: a landscape pad (Lens beat 8 of 16) also keeps nearby totems answered.

chapters.title: Walkthrough: stack Pulse Cairns
chapters.text:
Goal: buffer burst generators into a steady reserve.

You need
Pulse Cairns, a generator that spikes (Wake Bell or Drumheart), and a hungry machine.

Steps
1. Place a cairn beside the generator. It holds 4,000 Pulse and swallows up to 200 Pulse a second from nearby generators.
2. Stack up to five cairns in a column. The sixth stone is just a stone.
3. Put the hungry machine within 8 of the stack.
4. A comparator against a cairn reads how full it is.

Check
A Wake Bell burst fills the cairn, then the pit or workshop draws a steady line.

If it does not work
Both ends need to be loaded. Sneak-use this book on the cairn.

chapters.title: Walkthrough: light an Ember Horn
chapters.text:
Goal: turn furnace fuel into Pulse at the Drumhearts' craft.

You need
An Ember Horn (Drumheart tribe craft) and furnace fuel. Coal is enough to test.

Steps
1. Place the horn. Hopper or hand-feed fuel.
2. Burn time divided by twenty is Pulse, delivered at up to 20 a second. Coal is 80 Pulse, a lava bucket 1,000.
3. Unranked, the cap is 20 a second. More fuel does not raise it. Rank adds 15% Pulse a second per rank. Scale further by placing more horns.
4. A lever pauses it.

Check
Stored Pulse climbs while fuel burns. Empty-handed click names the remaining burn.

If it does not work
Horns are a tribe craft. Check standing and the recipe. Sneak-use this book on the horn.

chapters.title: Walkthrough: hang a Wind Harp
chapters.text:
Goal: harvest free Pulse from sky and weather.

You need
A Wind Harp (Pattern-weaver craft) and open sky.

Steps
1. Place the harp under open sky. Under a roof it makes nothing.
2. Base is 1 Pulse a second, plus 1 more under open sky; plus height (y 128 / y 192) and rain or storm. Six a second is the unranked cap. Rank adds 15% Pulse a second per rank.
3. Harps within twelve blocks divide the wind between them. One harp is the point.
4. A lever pauses it.

Check
An open-sky harp ticks Pulse. A second harp beside it splits the same wind.

If it does not work
Remove the roof. Check you are not standing in a cluster of harps.

chapters.title: Walkthrough: feed a Wave Drum
chapters.text:
Goal: make Pulse from water, then carry that water with the drum.

You need
A Wave Drum (Rootbinder craft) and a water source. A Spirit Cistern is better than a puddle.

Steps
1. Place the drum beside water for 3 Pulse a second, shared with any drum within 8.
2. Give it its own water instead — a bucket, a cistern, or a fluid relay — and it makes 10 a second for 100 mB a second.
3. Rain doubles either tier. Rank adds 15% Pulse a second per rank.
4. Break the drum: its internal 4,000 mB water tank stays on the dropped item. The drum holds 1,000 Pulse.

Check
Pulse rises, and water in the internal tank drops when it is feeding itself.

If it does not work
A dry drum is only the neighbour-water tier. Fill it. Sneak-use this book.

chapters.title: Walkthrough: seat a Wake Bell
chapters.text:
Goal: turn mob deaths into Pulse.

You need
A Wake Bell (Seal-carver craft) and a place hostiles die. A Ward Drum or a dark farm works.

Steps
1. Place the bell within 16 blocks of the deaths.
2. Twenty Pulse for a hostile death, five for a passive one. Reservoir 2,000, outflow at most 8 a second unranked. Rank adds 15% Pulse a second per rank.
3. Only the nearest bell hears a death. Stacking bells buys nothing.
4. Pair a Pulse Cairn if a Listening Pit wants a steady draw.

Check
A kill fills the reservoir, then Pulse leaks out at 8 a second unranked.

If it does not work
Move closer to the deaths. Players are never the target of a Ward Drum; the bell still hears the death.

chapters.title: Walkthrough: plant a Loom Anchor
chapters.text:
Goal: generate Pulse from how complete the camp already is.

You need
A Loom Anchor (Loom-stitcher craft) and several distinct totem voices within 8.

Steps
1. Place the anchor in the middle of your voices.
2. One Pulse a second per distinct voice within 8, to a maximum of six. Quiet totems still count.
3. A live Ley Binding nearby doubles it.
4. Kinship Totems lend the tribe's element into that six-voice set; they are not a seventh voice. Rank adds 15% Pulse a second per rank.

Check
Empty-handed click names the voice count and Pulse a second.

If it does not work
Voices have to stand within 8. Quiet totems still count; empty air does not. Sneak-use this book.

chapters.title: Walkthrough: run a Stone Font
chapters.text:
Goal: make cobblestone, then stone, then obsidian from Pulse. The font does not take cobble as an input.

You need
A Stone Font, Ritual Chalk, and a Drumheart within 8. Earth, Anchor Stones, and later Fire and Water or fluid pipes are for higher tiers.

Steps
1. Place the font. Draw four chalk marks around it on the same floor. Its slots are output only — do not hopper cobble in.
2. Keep a Drumheart in range. Unbraced, it produces cobble every two seconds at 4 Pulse a second. Earth is not required for cobble.
3. Brace the corners with Anchor Stones and keep Earth in reach for stone at 16 Pulse a second before pack settings.
4. Keep that brace. Fire and Water both: obsidian at 24 Pulse a second before pack settings. Or feed 250 mB water and 250 mB lava for the same obsidian at 6 before pack settings. Unbraced piping does nothing. Cobble stays 4; pack settings do not touch it.
5. Below y 0 it gives the deepslate of each tier instead. A pack pit-speed setting shortens every ask without raising Pulse a second, so it also cheapens each block.

Check
Cobble appears in the font with no cobble fed in. Braced Earth then produces stone.

If it does not work
The diagram in Patterns is the current shape. Ghosts show missing pieces. Sneak-use this book: it names missing marks or voices.

chapters.title: Walkthrough: dig a Listening Pit
chapters.text:
Goal: listen ore out of renewable stone.

You need
Stone or deepslate, four Anchor Stones, Ritual Chalk, a Resonance Mesh, an Ancestral Cache, Earth within 8, Pulse, and Friend standing with the Grit-singers.

Steps
1. Lay the floor. Brace four corners with Anchor Stones.
2. Chalk from each edge to the middle. Set the Resonance Mesh at the centre and the cache beside it.
3. Feed substrate from the sides. Seat a sample on top as a filter — it is not consumed.
4. Take ore from the bottom, or let the mesh empty into the cache.
5. Deep Listening (7x7, totems on the cardinals, a hearth or Grit-singer Kinship Totem inside) opens deeper bands. Kin standing for deep and hot; Voice plus Spirit for rare. Quartz needs Fire (the hot band), not the deep band.

Check
Stone in, raw metal or gem-ore out. The sample is still there.

If it does not work
Sneak-use this book on the mesh. Earth is required. Friend standing is required even for common. A sample the band does not hold is ignored.

chapters.title: Walkthrough: build a Voice Ring
chapters.text:
Goal: count six totem voices on one Resonator.

You need
A Pulse Resonator, a catalyst, and Resonance Totems of different voices.

Steps
1. Place the Resonator. Seat the catalyst.
2. On the same floor, three blocks away at the cardinals and diagonals, stand totems (eight slots).
3. Distinct voices among those arranged totems all count, including the sixth. Only Answered Resonance Totems count; Quiet voices do not.
4. A heap of totems beside the Resonator still works, but counts at most five total, kinship included. The ring is what lets six elements plus kinship add up.

Check
Sneak-use this book on the Resonator. It shows ghosts of missing ring slots and the voice count.

If it does not work
Totems must stand at radius 3, same level, and stay Answered. Two Earth totems are still one voice.

chapters.title: Walkthrough: brace a Shatter Array
chapters.text:
Goal: cheapen an Echo station and empty it into a cache.

You need
An Echo station, four totems of that recipe's attunement, an Ancestral Cache, and a 5x5 floor.

Steps
1. Centre the station. Put the cache beneath it.
2. Stand four matching totems at the corners of a five-by-five.
3. The station then costs a quarter less Pulse and empties itself into the cache.
4. Optional: every station still works without this brace.

Check
Output appears in the cache, not only in the station.

If it does not work
Wrong voice at a corner does nothing extra. Sneak-use this book.

chapters.title: Walkthrough: chain Attune and Bind
chapters.text:
Goal: walk shards to Bound Echoes without a hopper.

You need
Echo Attune, Echo Bind, Fire and Water totems, Echo Shards, and Pulse.

Steps
1. Place Attune with Fire within 8. Place Bind with Water within 8.
2. Sit Attune on Bind, or beside it. Set the touching faces to Output into Input.
3. Feed Echo Shards into Attune. Take Bound Echoes from Bind.
4. Bind also turns wool into Spiritweave and dirt into clay.
5. Sit Bind on Manifest for ingots and cores.

Check
Shards go in the top station; Bound Echoes come out the bottom.

If it does not work
Both-into-Both ping-pongs. Output into Input only. Check voices and Pulse.

chapters.title: Walkthrough: snap a cargo relay
chapters.text:
Goal: move items or fluid between two loaded machines.

You need
Two relay plates (Local is enough), a Bond item, and two inventories. A Lattice Tuner is the other pairing method.

Steps
1. Snap a plate onto a face of each machine. Relays are for distance; neighbours should use Output-into-Input.
2. Seat the same item in both Bond slots, or mark a destination face with the Lattice Tuner then use it on the plate. Do not mark the plate.
3. Water Seal in the Rune slot moves fluid, Earth Seal moves items; empty uses the plate name.
4. Sneak-click a plate to switch extract or insert.
5. Both ends must be loaded. Unloaded destinations pause; they do not void.

Check
Items (or fluid) move each second. Breaking the plate dumps Bond and Rune beside it; a tuner mark survives.

If it does not work
Hoppers cannot steal the Bond. Sneak-use this book on the plate.

chapters.title: Walkthrough: bind a Waystone Compass
chapters.text:
Goal: land on a marked floor.

You need
A Waystone Compass and a solid floor with two clear dry blocks above it.

Steps
1. Sneak-use the compass on the top of the floor to bind a landing.
2. Use it to return. Same world, 128 blocks, 20 Pulse.
3. Horizon Compass: any distance in one world, 40 Pulse. Astral Compass: across dimensions, 100 Pulse.
4. Power the landing floor with redstone to lock arrival. Five-second cooldown.

Check
You arrive standing on the bound floor. A blocked landing refuses and spends nothing.

If it does not work
Clear two blocks above the floor. Dry. Fill a Pulse Cell.

chapters.title: Walkthrough: convert Pulse to FE
chapters.text:
Goal: feed a standard energy machine from the lattice.

You need
A Pulse Adapter, a generator within 8, and an FE receiver.

Steps
1. Place the Adapter beside the generator and the FE machine.
2. It converts 1 Pulse into 100 FE, up to 20 Pulse each second. Ranked adapters convert more.
3. It buffers 16,000 FE and exports to standard energy receivers. It cannot receive FE.
4. Redstone stops conversion and extraction. A comparator reads the FE buffer.

Check
The FE machine runs. The Adapter's buffer is not empty.

If it does not work
No Pulse in range, or the receiver is full. Sneak-use this book.

chapters.title: Walkthrough: face an Ancestral Cache
chapters.text:
Goal: feed or drain a station with no hopper.

You need
An Ancestral Cache and an Echo station (or any machine with IO faces).

Steps
1. Place the cache beside or under the station.
2. Open it. The IO pad sets each face to Input, Output, Both or Closed. Sneak-empty-hand on a face does the same.
3. Set the touching faces to Output into Input. Both-into-Both does nothing, so stacks cannot ping-pong.
4. A lever locks access and automation. A comparator reads how full it is.

Check
The station takes from the cache or empties into it.

If it does not work
Check face settings. Hoppers still honour those faces.

chapters.title: Walkthrough: open a Deep Cache
chapters.text:
Goal: use one personal vault from any Deep Cache.

You need
A Deep Cache. Visiting The March attunes you; otherwise opening costs 5 Pulse.

Steps
1. Place a Deep Cache.
2. Open it. Every Deep Cache you place shares that 54-slot vault.
3. A Wayfarer Satchel opens the same vault. Sneak-use the satchel to switch to a shared camp vault.
4. A lever locks the block. The vault is not emptied by a pause.

Check
Put an item in one cache, walk, open another. The item is there.

If it does not work
Pay 5 Pulse or visit The March once. Camp vault is a different inventory.

chapters.title: Walkthrough: open the March
chapters.text:
Goal: walk into The March and come back.

You need
A Gate Drum, charged Pulse cells, food, and a bound return compass.

Steps
1. Place the Gate Drum. Charge it: a Pulse Cell adds up to 25 Pulse each use, or sneak-use empty-handed for 5 at a time. The drum holds 200. Travel costs 20 from that store, not from a cell in your pocket.
2. Bind a Waystone Compass to a dry floor at home before you leave.
3. Empty-handed use (not a Drumheart strike) walks you through. Redstone locks the drum.
4. Walk the biomes: Steppe, Highlands, Crystal Fields, Snow Fields, Ember Wastes, Reed Fen.
5. Read every tablet in an Ancestor Hall. Drum Circles stand in the highlands. Use the compass to return.

Check
You stand in The March, and the compass brings you home.

If it does not work
The drum needs 20 stored Pulse. A blocked landing refunds it. Clear two blocks above the floor. Sneak-use this book on the drum.

chapters.title: Walkthrough: pair Way Gates
chapters.text:
Goal: send players, mobs and items through a linked frame.

You need
Gate Frames, two Gate Keystones, Pulse, and a Waystone Compass or Ritual Chalk.

Steps
1. Build a five-by-five ring without its corners. Put the keystone at the bottom centre.
2. Charge it from a Pulse Cell (up to 100 Pulse each use), then light it by hand or with a struck signal: 400 Pulse out of its own 600.
3. Bind a Waystone Compass to the first keystone (sneak-use while unbound), then sneak-use that bound compass on the second. Chalk from one keystone to the other within 64 also works.
4. Twenty Pulse carries anything that walks in. A one-second cooldown stops bounce-back. The far end stays loaded ten seconds around arrival.
5. Far Gate is taller, Loom-voiced, linked with a Gate Sigil both ways. Lighting a Far Gate costs 1,200 Pulse out of its 2,000 store; travel is 120 with a two-second cooldown.

Check
Walk in; you land inside the partner's interior. /tribalpower gate list names the pair.

If it does not work
A blocked interior refuses and refunds Pulse. Break a keystone to release its partner.

chapters.title: Walkthrough: call a spring
chapters.text:
Goal: refill a Spirit Cistern without buckets.

You need
A Ritual Brazier, four Rite Pedestals, Ritual Chalk, the Water Seal, a Spring Calling tablet, 300 Pulse, and a Spirit Cistern beside the brazier.

Steps
1. Draw the circle: four Rite Pedestals on the diagonals, chalk joining them. Every tablet rite, including this one, refuses without it.
2. Seat the Water Seal in the brazier.
3. Place a Spirit Cistern beside it.
4. Sneak-use the tablet on the brazier. The cistern refills 100 mB a second for ten minutes.
5. Moving the cistern ends the spring; water already inside stays on the item.

Check
The cistern's mB climb on their own. You do not have to stand beside it.

If it does not work
Missing pedestals or chalk name the circle and spend nothing. No cistern beside the brazier also spends nothing.

chapters.title: Walkthrough: cast the Sixfold Staff
chapters.text:
Goal: pick a voice and cast it.

You need
A Sixfold Staff and a charged Pulse Cell.

Steps
1. Sneak-use to choose a voice. Use to cast.
2. Earth slows foes. Fire strikes and ignites for 4 seconds. Water heals and cleanses. Air grants a short leap and slow falling. Spirit reveals enemies within 12 blocks. Loom tethers a foe up to 8 blocks, or sneaking with no target stitches you 6 blocks forward.
3. Costs: Earth 12, Fire 18, Water 24, Air 16, Spirit 20; Loom 6 to tether, 10 to stitch.
4. Water rests 8 seconds; other voices 2. Stitch rests 1.5 seconds. Offensive spells reach 18 blocks and stop at solid obstacles.

Check
The action bar names the voice. Pulse drops by the listed cost.

If it does not work
Charge the cell. Loom stitch needs no target and a sneak.

chapters.title: Walkthrough: swing a Resonance Maul
chapters.text:
Goal: excavate a 3-by-3 of stone.

You need
A Resonance Maul in the main hand and Pulse.

Steps
1. Hold the maul. Sneak-use a stone face.
2. Each block costs 8 Pulse. Tool requirements and player protection still apply.
3. Totem-bound Earth picks open 3-by-3 the same way once linked.

Check
Nine stone (or fewer at an edge) break, and Pulse drops.

If it does not work
Wrong face, not enough Pulse, or the block needs a stronger tool.

chapters.title: Walkthrough: wear Spiritweave
chapters.text:
Goal: wear a boon and keep it fed.

You need
Spiritweave armor and Pulse.

Steps
1. Craft the cloth in Echo Bind (wool plus Water). Rank it Attune, Bind, Manifest like other gear.
2. Unlinked hood: night sight. Robe: resistance. Leggings: speed. Boots: slow falling when descending.
3. Unlinked pieces spend 2 Pulse every four seconds. A bound voice spends 3.
4. Sneak-use a piece on a placed Resonance Totem with 40 Pulse to replace that boon with the totem's voice.

Check
The boon is on, and Pulse ticks down while you wear it.

If it does not work
Unequip if the drum runs dry. Mixed voices are intended.

chapters.title: Walkthrough: rank a machine
chapters.text:
Goal: speed a workshop without skipping voices.

You need
The machine as an item, Echo Attune, Bind, Manifest, and their totems.

Steps
1. Pick up the machine. Seat the item in Echo Attune (Fire), then Bind (Water), then Manifest (Spirit).
2. Rank 1: 85% time, 118% Pulse. Rank 2: 70% and 143%. Rank 3: 55% and 182%. Machine stations cost twice Spiritgear: Attune 16s/48 Pulse a second, Bind 20s/64, Manifest 24s/80. Generators add 15% Pulse a second per rank, not this 118%.
3. You cannot skip. Bind refuses rank 0.
4. Place it again. The rank rides on the block and on the item when you pick it up.

Check
The tooltip names the rank. The station finishes faster and draws more Pulse.

If it does not work
Wrong station for the current rank. Sneak-use this book.

chapters.title: Walkthrough: wear a Spirit Charm
chapters.text:
Goal: wear one Tribal charm and know its cost.

You need
A crafted charm. Three slots — no other mod is required.

Steps
1. Use the charm to wear it. Sneak-use to open the three slots.
2. Sky is creative flight. Ember is fire. Tide is breath and swim. Root is resistance. Lantern is sight. Spindle is luck, and about three times in ten it refunds up to 2 Pulse into a carried cell every two seconds. Ward turns aside about one projectile in four, or one in two if Spirit is also on the charm. Hearth keeps you fed. Veil hides you while you sneak.
3. Chorus starts silent. Sneak-use it on a Ritual Brazier with three different totems within 8 and 200 Pulse to bind nearby voices. Extra sneak-uses on totems add voices for 40 Pulse each.
4. Worn cost is 2 Pulse per voice every two seconds. A silent Chorus still costs 2.

Check
The boon is on. Unequip if Pulse runs dry.

If it does not work
Sneak-use opens the slots. Chorus needs the brazier bind first.

chapters.title: Walkthrough: hush a camp
chapters.text:
Goal: stop new hostiles spawning around camp.

You need
A Hush Totem and Pulse.

Steps
1. Place it. It suppresses hostile spawning within 24 blocks for 8 Pulse a second.
2. A 2,400-Pulse reserve bridges interruptions; nearby generators refill up to 80 Pulse a second. It covers natural and spawner-born hostiles, including Summoning Cradles.
3. It does not remove existing mobs, stop animals, or override commands and spawn eggs.
4. Redstone silences the ward immediately. Keep a cradle outside the circle, or clock the totem.

Check
No new hostiles appear in the circle while Pulse flows.

If it does not work
Existing mobs stay. Light the camp as well. Sneak-use this book.

chapters.title: Walkthrough: plant a Wayanchor
chapters.text:
Goal: keep one chunk loaded.

You need
A Wayanchor and a generator that can spare 16 Pulse a second.

Steps
1. Place the anchor in the chunk you want held.
2. It spends 16 Pulse a second. A 2,400-Pulse reserve bridges interruptions; nearby generators refill up to 80 Pulse a second.
3. Up to 32 anchors may run per dimension. A shared camp budgets twelve.
4. Redstone or an empty reserve releases its ticket. Removing the block releases it immediately.

Check
Leave the area; a relay in that chunk still ticks.

If it does not work
Empty reserve, redstone pause, or the dimension cap. Sneak-use this book.

chapters.title: Walkthrough: catch with a Wind Snare
chapters.text:
Goal: pick items off the ground into a chest.

You need
A Wind Snare, Pulse, and a place items fall.

Steps
1. Place it near a farm, a shatter station, or a Grove Tender.
2. Keep 2 Pulse nearby per stack it catches, up to eight stacks a second, within 8 blocks.
3. Open it like a chest, or hopper the catch out of any face.
4. A lever pauses both the catch and the hoppers.

Check
Dropped wheat (or grit) appears in the snare, not on the floor.

If it does not work
It does not steal from other inventories. Only items on the ground.

chapters.title: Walkthrough: watch with a Ward Drum
chapters.text:
Goal: shove hostiles off the edge of camp.

You need
A Ward Drum and Pulse.

Steps
1. Place it where hostiles walk. It listens in an 8-block sphere.
2. Keep 8 Pulse nearby. Each second it hits one hostile for 4 magic and a shove.
3. Players are never the target.
4. A lever silences it. A comparator reads 15 on a hit, 0 while it waits.
5. Pair a Wake Bell if the deaths should pay Pulse back.

Check
A hostile in range is shoved. The comparator blinks 15.

If it does not work
Not a farm. One target a second. Sneak-use this book.

chapters.title: Walkthrough: reverse a Tide Pump
chapters.text:
Goal: move fluid between two tanks.

You need
A Tide Pump and two fluid tanks (Spirit Cisterns work). Pulse.

Steps
1. Place tanks on both faces. Do not use the pump as storage; breaking it does not keep a reserve.
2. The arrow face is the front. By default it draws from the front and pushes into the back.
3. Sneak-use to reverse.
4. Each second it moves 250 mB for 4 Pulse. A lever pauses it.
5. Click empty-handed to read the current direction.

Check
One cistern falls, the other rises, 250 mB a second.

If it does not work
Both tanks must accept the same fluid. Sneak-use this book.

chapters.title: Walkthrough: imprint a Binding Effigy
chapters.text:
Goal: remember a living spirit without harming it, then summon it.

You need
A Binding Effigy, an eligible creature, a Spirit Seal, Earth Air and Spirit totems, 200 Pulse, three Spiritweave, then a Summoning Cradle.

Steps
1. Sneak-use the empty or exhausted effigy on an eligible animal or hostile. Farm animals, zombies, skeletons, spiders, creepers and Tribal creatures can be imprinted; bosses cannot.
2. A live binding cannot be overwritten. Spend its threads first.
3. Seat a Spirit Seal in a Ritual Brazier. Place Earth, Air and Spirit totems within 8. Carry three Spiritweave.
4. Use the imprinted, exhausted effigy on the brazier with redstone off. The three voices knot 512 summoning threads into it.
5. Place the bound effigy in a Summoning Cradle's first slot and Spiritweave in the second. Every ten seconds it spends 80 Pulse, one Spiritweave and one thread on a clear, dry floor within three blocks. Eight nearby mobs pause it. Keep a Hush Totem off the cradle if you still want peace in camp.

Check
The effigy tooltip names the imprint and remaining threads. The cradle summons without you standing there.

If it does not work
An imprint alone has no summons. The brazier names missing voices, Pulse or Spiritweave.

chapters.title: Walkthrough: look through a Ley Lens
chapters.text:
Goal: see ley, Pulse, voices and machines.

You need
A Ley Lens (glass, Copper Resonator, Spirit Shard).

Steps
1. Hold it and use it to cycle four sights: ley on the ground, the Pulse zone, nearby totem voices, and Tribal machines.
2. Sneak-use it on a Ley Collector for that collector's factor breakdown.
3. Sneak-use it on a lattice animal or remnant to print threads and Marks.
4. Voice mode tints totems gold when answered, dull when dim, grey when quiet.

Check
The ground tints. A sneak-use prints numbers in chat.

If it does not work
Hold it in either hand. Cycle until the right sight.

chapters.title: Walkthrough: craft a Kinship Totem
chapters.text:
Goal: add one tribe's voice to the Resonator.

You need
Voice standing (800) with that tribe, the Tribe Mark the Elder hands over, that tribe's Resonance Totem, and two Spiritweave.

Steps
1. Reach Voice at a Tribe Hearth. The Elder gives a Tribe Mark once.
2. Craft the Mark with the tribe's Resonance Totem and two Spiritweave.
3. Place the Kinship Totem within 8 of a Pulse Resonator. It is an extra tribe voice there. On a Loom Anchor or workshop it only fills that tribe's element. A heap still caps at five total; a Voice Ring lets six elements plus all nine tribes add up to fifteen.
4. A Grit-singer Kinship Totem or a Tribe Hearth inside Deep Listening is required for the deep, hot and rare bands, not only rare. Voice standing still gates the rare band.

Check
The Resonator names the extra voice. The Mark is spent into the totem.

If it does not work
Guest and Friend are not enough. Trade and offer until Voice.

chapters.title: Walkthrough: set an Offering Table
chapters.text:
Goal: keep a 27-slot store beside a hearth or cradle.

You need
An Offering Table. Hoppers or pipes are optional.

Steps
1. Place it beside a hearth or a cradle. It is storage, not a second Tribe Hearth.
2. Open it. Twenty-seven slots. Hoppers and item pipes insert or extract from every side.
3. A comparator reads fullness. A lever locks both the menu and automation.
4. No Pulse is needed. Offerings that raise tribe standing go on the Tribe Hearth.

Check
Items stay in the table. A hopper can fill or empty it. Standing is not granted here.

If it does not work
Redstone locks access. It does not take favoured items for standing — that is the hearth.

chapters.title: Walkthrough: hang a Rain Chime
chapters.text:
Goal: turn rain and thunder into a redstone tell.

You need
A Rain Chime and a comparator.

Steps
1. Place the chime where a comparator can read it. Weather is world-wide; a roof does not mute the signal.
2. It sounds softly every ten seconds during rain. No Pulse and no fuel.
3. Comparator: 8 for rain, 15 for thunder, 0 for clear skies.
4. A lever mutes it and sets the output to zero. Use the signal to pause a Ley Collector or light camp.

Check
It rains; the comparator reads 8. Thunder reads 15.

If it does not work
Redstone is muting it. It does not make Pulse by itself.

chapters.title: Walkthrough: hang a Spirit Lantern
chapters.text:
Goal: light camp at level 15 without fuel.

You need
A Spirit Lantern.

Steps
1. Place it along paths between workshops. It lights at 15. No Pulse is needed.
2. A lever dims it. A comparator reports whether it is lit.
3. Pair it with a Hush Totem: light plus hush is a quiet camp.

Check
The area is lit. A lever turns the light off.

If it does not work
It is a light, not a ward. Hostiles still need hush or light to stop spawning.

chapters.title: Walkthrough: tune Verse Call and Answer
chapters.text:
Goal: send redstone 32 blocks with no vine.

You need
A Verse Call, a Verse Answer, and a redstone source.

Steps
1. Snap the Call onto a face. It reads redstone from every side except its facing.
2. Snap the Answer onto a face within 32 blocks, same world. It sings out of its facing.
3. Sneak-use either plate to cycle verse 1 to 16. Both must match.
4. Several Calls of one verse: the Answer takes the loudest.

Check
Power the Call; the Answer copies that strength (15 if the Call heard 15). Mismatched verses stay silent.

If it does not work
Same world, 32 blocks, same verse. Relays still move items; these plates move only redstone.

chapters.title: Walkthrough: pause on a Pulse Threshold
chapters.text:
Goal: hush a machine when Pulse runs low.

You need
A Pulse Threshold, an Inverse plate, Song Thread, and a generator. A Pulse Gauge is optional.

Steps
1. Point a Pulse Gauge at a Drumheart, Resonator or cell-holding machine. It emits 0 to 15 from every face except the arrow.
2. Point a Pulse Threshold the same way. Empty-handed use cycles 25, 50, 75, 100 percent. It emits while stored Pulse is at or above that percent.
3. A held signal pauses machines, so a live Threshold would hush them while they still have Pulse. Run Inverse on that line so 'too empty' is the live signal.
4. Test with a hungry station before wiring the whole camp.

Check
When Pulse drops below the threshold, Inverse sings and the machine pauses. When it recovers, Inverse hushes and work resumes.

If it does not work
Facing and support matter. Direct Threshold-to-machine pauses on a full drum. Read Pulse logic.

chapters.title: Walkthrough: crawl a Song Vine
chapters.text:
Goal: carry redstone around a corner on stone, without a relay.

You need
Song Vine (one Song Thread and a Spirit Reed make eight), a solid block, and a redstone source.

Steps
1. Click a solid face. The vine sits in the air cell on that face.
2. Click that vine with another vine to add a second face on the same cell — floor and wall, or every side of a cube.
3. Power decays by one per step, including around corners onto a neighbouring face.
4. It speaks to Song Thread, song plates, vanilla dust and comparators. Relays still move items; vines carry only the song.
5. Break the host block to pick up one vine per face.

Check
A lever on one face lights a lamp around the corner. Strength drops by one per step.

If it does not work
The vine must sit on a solid face. Mismatched Song Thread still works; a roof does not mute it.

Next
Read Song Thread, then Walkthrough: a song clock.

chapters.title: Walkthrough: smelt in an Ember Kiln
chapters.text:
Goal: smelt with Pulse instead of coal. Cobble becomes stone; grit becomes an ingot.

You need
An Ember Kiln, a Fire Resonance Totem, a charged generator within 8, and cobble or grit.

Steps
1. Place the Kiln. Fire totem within 8. Keep Pulse in range.
2. Put cobble in the input. Take stone from the output. No coal is burned. Each smelt is 10 seconds at 32 Pulse a second before pack settings.
3. Optional chain: Echo Shatter with Earth nearby. Feed raw iron for grit (stone still makes shards, cobble makes gravel). Sit Shatter on the Kiln, Output into Input.
4. Take the ingot from the Kiln. Hopper or cache under it if you want.

Check
Cobble becomes stone. Grit becomes an ingot. Missing Fire pauses and spends nothing.

If it does not work
Full output pauses. Crouch and right-click this book on the Kiln.

Next
Read Walkthrough: seat a Resonator for automatic Pulse.

chapters.title: Walkthrough: unweave a lattice product
chapters.text:
Goal: reverse a lattice product at Echo Unweave.

You need
Echo Unweave, a Loom Resonance Totem, Pulse within 8, and a lattice product (Manifested Ingot, Resonant Core, Spiritweave, or damaged Spiritgear).

Steps
1. Place Echo Unweave. Loom totem within 8.
2. Feed a Manifested Ingot for 2 Bound Echoes, a Resonant Core for 3 Manifested Ingots, Spiritweave for wool, or damaged Spiritgear for one Manifested Ingot. Fresh undamaged tools refuse Unweave.
3. Keep Pulse in range and output space free.
4. Rank the station in Echo Attune, Bind, then Manifest if you want it faster.

Check
The input is consumed and the reversed product sits in the output. Missing Loom pauses and spends nothing.

If it does not work
Sneak-use this book on the station. Fresh Spiritgear must take damage first. Read The sixth voice.

Next
Read The sixth voice, then Walkthrough: wear Spiritweave.

chapters.title: Dawn Stag
chapters.text: A dawn grazer that carries the old forest song in its antlers. Breed with wheat; brush adults for Dawn Velvet. Bond an adult with a Bonding Charm to ride it without a saddle.

chapters.title: Lantern Fox
chapters.text: A shy dusk forager whose tail marks safe paths. Breed with sweet berries; brush adults for Lantern Down. Bond an adult with a Bonding Charm for a lantern that follows you.

chapters.title: Mossback
chapters.text: A patient wetland gardener with a living shell. Breed with seagrass; brush adults for a naturally shed Mossback Scale. Bond an adult with a Bonding Charm for a walking saddlebag.

chapters.title: Ashbound
chapters.text: The remains of a broken fire rite. Its melee strikes briefly ignite; keep water close.

chapters.title: Rootbound
chapters.text: A grove guardian twisted by a severed ley line. Slow but sturdy; its blows root travellers briefly.

chapters.title: Reed Stalker
chapters.text: A marsh hunter concealed among spirit reeds. Fast strikes carry a short poison.

chapters.title: Shardback
chapters.text: A crystal-field scavenger armored in singing stone. Keep your distance from its heavy shove.

chapters.title: Hollow Sentinel
chapters.text: An empty watchman that still guards the ancient roads. Its touch weakens the grip of attackers.

chapters.title: Storm Moth
chapters.text: A storm-fed spirit with vast veil wings. A bright gathering of motes warns of its gust; cover breaks the attack.

chapters.title: Cinder Imp
chapters.text: A nimble ember spirit. It gathers sparks before a burning bolt; the spell never ignites terrain.

chapters.title: Mourning Bell
chapters.text: A floating relic that remembers the lost tribes. Its telegraphed chime slows; shelter interrupts the song.

chapters.title: Rift Hound
chapters.text: A hunter drawn to tears in the lattice. It closes distance quickly but cannot cross worlds by itself.

chapters.title: Echo Weaver
chapters.text: An eight-legged keeper of broken songs. Its bite slows prey without placing webs or damaging the camp.
